entries.summary: Redeven owns the Flower companion content presentation; released Floe owns its shell geometry and motion phases. One native composer retains its draft, selection, focus and IME through every presentation change. Expanded text sits above a bottom toolbar whose left side stays empty; permission, model and reasoning remain in More during loading and model failures. Guidance and recovery actions sit above the editor rather than competing with toolbar space. Closing detail dissolves before the compact layout appears, and reversal follows the current shell phase without remounting an editor or adding lifecycle timers. Specialized decisions retain their controls. [Flower Activity companion](flower-activity-companion.md) owns placement, dismissal, focus handoffs and read acknowledgement.

entries.title: Flower companion presence
entries.description: Project canonical Flower work into the compact companion without displacing drafts, stealing focus, or creating another lifecycle owner.
entries.summary: Redeven projects canonical Floret summaries and matching current-run detail into one compact Flower status. Active work, pending actions, and user-owned drafts retain explicit precedence; historical completion never masquerades as new feedback. Presence shares the existing workspace stream and does not auto-expand, claim transcript reads, or recreate thread lifecycle state. A disconnect follows the existing transport refresh contract. [Flower Activity companion](flower-activity-companion.md) owns placement, native composer identity, dismissal, and read acknowledgement.

entries.title: Flower read state
entries.description: Keep unread indicators monotonic and acknowledge only rendered content through silent background recovery.
entries.summary: Redeven owns per-user read confirmation. Unread indicators compare current activity with server confirmation and actual local presentation. Old responses never restore a dot for an already read version; new unseen activity remains unread. Temporary synchronization failures recover silently in the background, without blocking any user operation.

entries.title: Flower incremental live state
entries.description: One workspace stream, actor-native updates, and one indexed ThreadCache.
entries.summary: Floret owns runtime state, canonical history, item identity and view versions. Redeven authorizes and projects public data; one workspace stream delivers it to ThreadCache. Ordinary text growth carries only the changed item and its UTF-8 append offset. It must not copy, scan, redact, encode or rebuild the complete history. Missing authority or a broken sequence invalidates observation and refreshes summaries plus the required current view through the existing connection owner. Execution and user drafts survive that recovery.

entries.title: Flower file edit preparation
entries.description: Show candidate filenames while tool arguments stream without authorizing or executing edits.
entries.summary:
Flower shows candidate filenames while file-editing arguments are being prepared.
The existing Floret argument preview is display-only; actual tool results remain
the authority for completed changes. Progressive names keep long preparations
understandable while one stable activity row continues through approval and
execution.

entries.title: Flower timeline ordering
entries.description: Canonical typed views, separate submission feedback, and stable row identity.
entries.summary: Flower renders the ordered items in Floret's typed current view. Canonical stable IDs plus each item's exact TurnID and RunID determine user, assistant, tool, interaction, queue, and terminal rows. Ordinary unconfirmed input remains in the composer with Send button loading. A short-lived transport outbox shows queued submissions only in the queue dock; matching canonical request-key confirmation updates that same row without duplicating the transcript. Summaries never write timeline detail.

entries.title: Flower terminal turn process disclosure
entries.description: Collapse historical and successful work while protecting current abnormal work, explicit choices and active reading.
entries.summary:
Published Floret owns turn identity, outcome, final output and durations. Flower
uses validated detail only. Successful ordinary turns default to collapsed; the
latest failed, cancelled or interrupted turn stays expanded, while older
abnormal turns collapse after newer work starts. Dialogue, answered inputs and
final segments stay ordered and visible; unknown output is never hidden. Pending
interactions stay expanded, and reading protection preserves the reader's
position. If an answered input falls between process rows in a settled turn,
Flower shows a static overview and keeps the receipt as a visible checkpoint.
Settled tool sequences on either side default to independent collapsed groups;
active tools remain available. Ordinary turns keep whole-turn disclosure.

entries.title: Flower reasoning selection ownership
entries.description: Preserve explicit reasoning choices across cold loads, shared drafts, submission, and restart.
entries.summary: Confirmed Thread settings own the reasoning level displayed for an existing Flower conversation. Drafts own only explicit new-thread choices; computed defaults never become draft intent. Default reasoning is a configuration choice, not an enabled state or an effort level. Cold loading and restart preserve explicit Off and On. Controls reflect verified model capabilities; unknown controls remain model-controlled. Failed saves retain the confirmed setting, and active Turns retain their immutable runtime configuration.

entries.title: Flower personal conversation preferences
entries.description: Remember explicit model, directory, and model-owned reasoning choices without importing thread settings into future defaults.
entries.summary:
Flower remembers explicit choices for future root conversations in one
Redeven-owned product store, scoped by authenticated namespace, endpoint, and
user. The existing controls and layout are unchanged. Loading or switching a
Thread never writes a preference. Existing Threads and immutable Turns keep
their own confirmed settings; new conversations use explicit launch/draft
choices before personal memory and configured defaults.

entries.title: Flower model and navigation presentation
entries.description: Model-source controls, notifications, thread selection, and staged content ownership.
entries.summary: Flower keeps environment and Desktop model sources explicit, preserves thread-owned model and reasoning defaults, and keeps unavailable selections distinct from first-time setup. Thread selection separates immediate visual intent from committed content and rejects stale loads. Transient operation failures use host notifications instead of transcript content, while canonical run and tool failures stay with their owning timeline renderers.

entries.title: Flower setup and settings
entries.description: First-time model setup, actionable starter tasks, and shared provider, permission, and computer settings.
entries.summary:
The shared Flower surface owns setup and settings for Desktop and Env App.
An empty profile without a usable model or selected conversation offers explicit
setup actions. Configured new conversations offer starter tasks as editable
drafts; selecting one never launches a turn. Settings use flat sections and
preserve drafts, model-source identity and permission ownership. Connection
failures and configured profiles needing repair retain their recovery controls.
Settings open in a shared modal dialog over the mounted chat. Background chat
and navigation stay visible but inert until the dialog finishes closing; covered
chat does not acknowledge reads. Settings save progress and errors survive hiding.

entries.title: Flower provider configuration
entries.description: Configure provider access before choosing models, with stable navigation and explicit authentication states.
entries.summary:
One shared Flower provider dialog owns provider configuration in Desktop,
embedded Flower and global Env settings; hosts own admission and persistence.
Users choose a provider, supply required connection access, and then configure
models. Unready ChatGPT authorization exposes connection actions only. Provider
navigation, authentication selection, and model rows retain stable geometry and
focus. Failed authorization or discovery keeps recovery actions visible and must
not apply responses from a changed provider or trusted connection.

entries.title: Flower ChatGPT authentication
entries.description: Select, reauthorize, sign out and remove local ChatGPT accounts with stable interaction and explicit intent.
entries.summary:
The shared [Flower provider dialog](flower-provider-configuration.md) owns account
selection and authentication feedback. Signed-in accounts remain distinct from
previous connections, sign-out preserves a stable compact summary, and explicit
removal forgets only a signed-out local registration. The host retains verified
local admission and persistence ownership.

entries.title: Flower failure recovery
entries.description: One turn-level failure owner and bounded manual recovery without replaying uncertain effects.
entries.summary:
Floret owns canonical execution outcomes and retry checkpoints. Flower keeps
accepted messages readable and provides one turn-level failure and recovery
surface. Navigation, settings exit, drafts and queue editing remain available.
Transport uncertainty never proves backend success or authorizes replay.
Readiness timeouts use the shared bounded request helpers and expose a status
refresh without replaying Prepare or Stop. Deterministic migration failures
remain diagnostic/admin recovery states; supported compaction history is
automatically migrated by published Floret v7.74.0 through schema 29. See
[historical compatibility](../ai/flower-upgrade-compatibility.md).

entries.title: Flower composer attachments
entries.description: Connection-local attachment staging, long-text conversion, and canonical timeline presentation.
entries.summary:
- Authority: Flower owns connection-local editing, its host adapter owns authenticated staging transport, Redeven owns staged bytes and unadmitted commands, and Floret owns admitted attachment history.
- Outcome: file selection, drag-and-drop, paste, progress, retry, removal, preview, reference copy, attachment-only send, and long-text restore behave consistently in Activity, Workbench, Desktop, and mobile layouts.
- Invariants: text is converted only above 50,000 Unicode code points, IME composition is never interrupted, and source text is not cleared until staging succeeds.
- Failure boundary: invalid Unicode, capability drift, quota, upload, restore, or pre-acceptance failure preserves the connection-local editor and never synthesizes user text.

entries.title: Flower file activity presentation
entries.description: Typed file mutation statistics, diff disclosure, and action ownership.
entries.summary:
Flower presents confirmed file reads and mutations from canonical typed Floret
Activity. [Received output progress](flower-output-progress.md) owns temporary
argument-generation counts before those outcomes exist. A mutation row shows the user-facing file name and aggregate added and
deleted line counts; its detail contains the matching unified diff. Protocol
fields, unrelated private paths never become display metadata. Explicit navigation targets
are historical facts, not current read authority.
An activity without typed mutation detail exposes safe purpose and status through
the shared disclosure, without inventing a diff panel.

entries.title: Flower consecutive tool sequences
entries.description: Compact tools and bounded thinking without hiding dialogue or taking over active reading.
entries.summary:
Flower groups consecutive tool calls in the shared Desktop and Env App timeline.
Thinking after the first tool becomes an inline node in that sequence, including
thinking after the final tool. Older settled sequences collapse while the newest
sequence and active tools remain expanded.
When an answered input falls between work segments in a settled turn, each
settled tool sequence remains independently collapsed, including the newest
sequence. Active tools retain their existing disclosure behavior.
This is product presentation over existing published Floret facts; it introduces
no upstream contract, canonical summary or backend migration.

entries.title: Flower activity disclosure interaction
entries.description: Keep native tool activation, disclosure state, viewport following, and floating controls consistent during live updates.
entries.summary:
Flower owns activity interaction in its shared UI. Canonical Floret identity and
presentation remain the only execution facts. Each transcript has one viewport
controller for follow intent, user input, temporary anchoring, and position
writes. A live update must not move a pressed tool trigger or introduce a
floating hit target before its native click completes. Canceled gestures never
activate tools. All transient ownership ends when its view is disposed.

entries.title: Flower conversation sidebar
entries.description: Select conversations clearly and reorder endpoint-owned pins without interrupting live interactions.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns conversation selection presentation and persistent pin order. Desktop
and Env App use the same Flower sidebar. Selection, running activity, unread
attention and pending replies or approvals retain independent meanings. Live summary changes
must preserve row identity, open menus, focus and running wave continuity. Pin
failures undo only the current operation's presentation and reconcile through the
existing workspace summary stream or one explicit post-command read.

entries.title: Flower inline media
entries.description: Display assistant media through released Floe previews and authorized Runtime resources.
entries.summary:
Flower displays assistant images, screenshots, video, audio, and self-contained
HTML directly in the conversation. Released Floe chat components own media
presentation and HTML isolation. Redeven owns resource routing and permission
checks; Floret's canonical message remains the only durable display source.
Unavailable, forbidden, oversized, or mismatched resources show a retryable
preview error without interrupting the conversation.

entries.title: Flower streaming stability
entries.description: Incremental Markdown and local record updates preserve interactive identity.
entries.summary: Flower renders actor-native changes through the indexed ThreadCache and the published Floe incremental Markdown parser. Ordinary growth changes the affected text/DOM region only. Stable history, code colors, copy controls, focus, selection and disclosure choices remain intact. A semantic change must remain visible; malformed updates recover through the single [live-state boundary](flower-live-timeline.md), never by omitting output or substituting a second lifecycle.

entries.title: Flower received output progress
entries.description: Request-scoped output estimates, model waiting time, and safe streamed edit statistics.
entries.summary:
Flower shows how long a dispatched model request has waited and how much output
has arrived. Edit rows show line counts while their arguments are generated,
then use the confirmed tool result. Published Floret v7.42.0 owns the generic
in-memory progress and preview lifecycle; Redeven interprets its own tool JSON
and presents the safe observations. No new journal records or schema changes
are required.

entries.title: Flower code highlighting
entries.description: Color stable Markdown code without disturbing streaming, selection, copy or layout.
entries.summary:
Flower owns Markdown parsing and committed segment lifetime. Published Floe
`enhanceCodeBlock` owns visible-code tokenization, scheduling and color application.
Completed language-labelled fences receive syntax colors in both Env App and
Desktop. Original code remains immediately readable and copyable. Highlighting
must not alter text, frame geometry, copy controls, focus or an active selection;
unavailable or excessive highlighting work leaves plain code visible.

entries.title: Flower message appearance
entries.description: Keep assistant reading and sent user messages readable in every shell theme without changing content or interaction.
entries.summary:
Flower owns transcript message presentation in the shared Env App and Desktop
UI. Published Floe theme tokens own the palette. Sent user messages use the
theme's text-selection accent with readable foreground text. Native selection
must remain visible within a filled bubble and its insets. Theme changes alter
paint only, preserving message DOM, geometry and active selection. Queued input
keeps its quieter pending presentation; forced colors use system roles.
Transcript messages retain their original compact reading scale; composer
controls retain the published control scale. Source destinations and copy follow
[Flower citations](flower-citations.md), including safe authored bibliographies.

entries.title: Flower terminal activity presentation
entries.description: Terminal output, truthful result messages, safe input confirmation, and read-only controls.
entries.summary: Flower renders canonical Floret v7 Activity facts. Host-authored labels and descriptions explain the task; every terminal operation has safe expandable details, including writes and empty reads. Disclosure and output scrolling are local presentation state. They never create process lifecycle facts or expose stdin, private working paths, or effect internals. Actionable approval controls belong to the composer.

entries.title: Flower interactions and context state
entries.description: Typed pending interactions, automatic context compression, and unlocked composer behavior.
entries.summary: Approval and waiting-user prompts are projections of Floret typed pending interactions. The bottom action mode is one mutually exclusive surface with fixed priority `input_request` then `approval` then `chat`, while the ordinary thread rail always remains interactive; decision surfaces never make a shared ancestor inert or install a pointer-blocking overlay.

entries.title: Asynchronous layout stability
entries.description: Keep controls and retained content stationary through pending work, feedback, and media decoding.
entries.summary: Floe owns reusable control geometry; Redeven owns the localized states and feedback placement of its product surfaces. Starting or finishing a request, copying a value, refreshing retained data, and decoding media must not push adjacent controls or content. Normal views stay compact without empty feedback rows. Blocking errors remain visible, and retained-content errors remain accessible through a compact disclosure in an existing action row. User navigation, explicit disclosure, and newly added records may change layout; asynchronous feedback must not simulate those actions.

entries.title: Shared interface scale
entries.description: Apply one measured desktop reading and control scale across Flower, Env App, and Desktop without shrinking content viewers or touch targets.
entries.summary: Published Floe owns typography, control dimensions, responsive targets, settings geometry, and virtual file row measurements. Redeven maps product roles to that released scale across Flower, Files, Git, runtime settings, monitoring, services, plugins, Codespaces, and Desktop Welcome. At a browser-controlled 16px root and 100% zoom, desktop body text is 12px/20px and conversation titles are 13px/20px; ordinary host navigation remains 12px/18px, and ordinary single-line rows occupy 28px including inter-row spacing. Touch and enlarged-text layouts grow naturally. No density preference, root-font reduction, transform scaling, or second theme state controls this behavior. A geometry failure is repaired at its owning component without changing permission, focus, draft, or scroll authority.

entries.title: Flower approval surface
entries.description: Review bounded approval queues, inspect exact commands, and submit independent or atomic one-time decisions.
entries.summary: Flower projects approvals from Floret typed current views through one compact list shared by Activity, the full page, Workbench, and Desktop. The actual chat container bounds the list while its header and decision footer remain visible. Approval identity, permissions, and completion remain canonical runtime concerns; local state owns disclosure and submission feedback only. Failures preserve the pending content and allow retry without blocking Stop or navigation.

entries.title: Flower citations
entries.description: Canonical assistant source ownership, safe links, and provider marker presentation.
entries.summary:
- Authority: published Floret v7.32.0 assistant messages own durable sources; Flower reads current views and historical pages through the existing thread projection.
- Outcome: provider citation markers in prose become readable links with source titles. Copying a message removes those markers.
- Invariants: ranges use end-exclusive Unicode code-point indices in the exact assistant text. URLs must be HTTP(S), without credentials, whitespace or control characters. Marker identifiers never establish a URL.
- Failure boundary: unmatched sources appear at the end of the completed message. Historical provider markers without stored sources show localized unavailable text; Flower never reconstructs missing provider facts. Explicit Markdown bibliographies remain authored content.

entries.title: Flower subagent detail window
entries.description: Stable parent-scoped child current views, live replacement, and queued-input controls.
entries.summary: The child detail window reads the complete canonical Floret `ThreadView`. HTTP and live updates share the selected parent-child identity, while Activity and queued-input controls remain attached to the same canonical child. The window preserves navigation and scroll state across updates without creating a second transcript or lifecycle owner.

entries.title: Flower subagent detail presentation
entries.description: Parent header membership, canonical thread routing, and child execution detail and canonical input controls.
entries.summary:
- Authority: Floret v7 parent-scoped `ThreadRuntime.List` owns child membership; the child's complete `ThreadView` is the only detail-content authority.
- Outcome: Flower opens a stable, parent-scoped detail window immediately and updates it live without polling or layout-changing sync chrome.
- Invariants: every public child route uses canonical `thread_id`; `task_name` is required and never guessed from title, role, description, or message.
- Failure boundary: malformed summaries, missing canonical identity, parent-child mismatch, or invalid detail contracts are rejected rather than mapped through legacy aliases.

entries.title: Flower parent event timeline
entries.description: Important child reports and automatic events in the parent conversation with canonical avatars and compact source navigation.
entries.summary:
- Authority: Floret owns received events and their canonical context admission; the UI holds only presentation pages, report bodies and disclosure state.
- Outcome: important child reports and automatic events appear directly in the selected parent conversation without opening the subagent dropdown.
- Invariants: every event uses the canonical child avatar; receipt, admission and preservation notices do not appear in the timeline. Reading never wakes either task.
- Failure boundary: recipient authorization and canonical fixed-range paging apply to every full read.

entries.title: Tessiven Runtime discovery and operations
entries.description: Discover scoped Runtime paths and delegate explicit connection, business access, and native process operations to their existing owners.
entries.summary:
The Runtime-owned Tessiven product service is the authority for UI and Flower
Runtime discovery and dispatch. It composes the existing Desktop connection
registry, authenticated Gateway catalogs, Runtime business resource executors,
and Desktop lifecycle coordinator. Discovery observes registered paths without
starting a process or acquiring a business session. A reference identifies one
path; it grants no permission. Lost source authority, changed path generations,
replaced identities, and revoked permissions stop dispatch. A lost mutation
response reports an uncertain canonical tool outcome. The model first inspects
the original operation or current state before deciding what work remains; the
original invocation never replays automatically.

entries.title: Tessiven Flower and operations
entries.description: Generate canvas versions and route service actions through their original owners.
entries.summary:
Flower maps authorized code, configuration, and connected Runtime facts into
Tessiven versions through the `redeven-tessiven` system skill. Flower owns canvas
content editing as a core workflow. Resource actions
remain owned by the existing Managed Services and Containers managers. A
transport failure after a mutation is dispatched is terminal with an unknown
outcome, so the user must inspect the original manager before trying again.

entries.title: Authorized platform model gateway
entries.description: Session-scoped platform catalogs, credential boundaries, stable request identity, and background execution.
entries.summary: Redeven AI uses the trusted control channel's platform lease and gateway origin to discover authorized models. The Runtime never receives a platform Provider API key. Floret continues to own thread execution, tools, canonical history, and recovery; the platform Edge owns authorization, binding, reservations, and final accounting.

entries.title: Model directory and selection
entries.description: Read configured model metadata immediately and make Provider inventory refresh an explicit opt-in without changing user intent.
entries.summary: The Runtime owns synchronization and atomic metadata snapshots. Reads and send preflight use shipped or saved metadata without waiting for supplier inventory. Failed or pending refresh never blocks configured chat. Background refresh is off by default, disclosed, and excludes OpenRouter. Adding OpenRouter/Ollama discovers their models; manual refresh remains available. Floret execution and storage contracts are unchanged.

entries.title: Model web search
entries.description: Resolve provider and model search intent once for settings, admission, and provider transport.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns provider and model search preferences. One backend resolver supplies
settings projections and Turn preparation; the final tool surface drives prompts
and wire declarations. Floret v7.40.2 validates hosted events against the actual
frozen provider request. Undeclared hosted execution remains a provider failure
because its remote effects cannot be assumed absent.

entries.title: Local ChatGPT plan authentication
entries.description: Admit official ChatGPT sign-in only through verified local host access and preserve provider history, credentials and billing choice.
entries.summary:
OpenAI connections have one active authentication method: API key or ChatGPT
account. Omitted authentication fields retain API-key behavior. ChatGPT uses
OpenAI's public open-source sign-in and `/v1/responses` contracts; it never reads
Codex credentials or calls a private ChatGPT backend. Floret v7.30.0 owns the
engine, canonical conversation, provider-state lifecycle and compaction. Redeven
owns account admission, protected credentials, provider configuration and UI.
Verified local admission is mandatory, billing choice never changes silently,
and private or remote callers cannot obtain account credentials. Account-lifecycle
failures remain explicit through the canonical owner linked below.

entries.title: ChatGPT account lifecycle
entries.description: Persist verified local sign-ins, reuse issued registrations and complete renewal, cancellation and logout independently of connection editing.
entries.summary:
Redeven's canonical protected account store owns verified ChatGPT registrations
and sessions. Returning setup reuses saved registrations; only explicit new-account
or workspace intent creates another. Email is never a registration or workspace
key. OAuth completion persists sign-in independently of connection
editing; identity-only grants never admit inference. Retry reuses issued client
identity with fresh OAuth inputs. Renewal and logout serialize rotating tokens.
Cancellation never installs usable credentials after its commit boundary, and
interrupted cleanup uses the existing durable logout journal. Storage failure
stops account use; local cleanup and remote revocation remain separate outcomes.
Local admission is owned by the [authentication contract](chatgpt-local-authentication.md).

entries.title: Provider configuration validation
entries.description: Apply provider-specific optional fields and reject incomplete model configurations before saving.
entries.summary: Redeven owns provider configuration, credential requirements, and Flower readiness. Ollama and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints can send without a stored key; other local-profile providers require one. All settings entrypoints and the provider-bundle API enforce configuration completeness without inventing stored secrets. Invalid saves leave configuration and credentials unchanged; network or authentication failures remain execution errors. Floret's published thread-runtime contract is unchanged.

entries.title: Provider API and catalog review
entries.description: Match the shipped model catalog to official APIs, regional endpoints, and released adapter capabilities.
entries.summary: Redeven owns one model catalog shared by Runtime, Web, Desktop, and the native iOS client through the authenticated catalog API. Official provider documentation establishes model identities, API contracts, and capability corrections; the pinned models.dev snapshot supplies reproducible inventory metadata. A model must be supported by the released adapter before it becomes selectable. Catalog refreshes preserve user selections and never replace a conversation's stored model. Unsupported engine capabilities remain explicit integration blockers.

entries.title: Direct image reading and tool media retention
entries.description: Authorized image reads produce immutable native model attachments with canonical retention and preview membership.
entries.summary:
`image.read(file_path, target_id)` reads an image directly in every permission
mode. Its exclusive `locator` mode rereads an admitted immutable snapshot in the
current thread without reopening the original file or copying bytes. Redeven
owns authorization and immutable bytes; Floret owns the typed
attachment, model history and canonical membership. File references stay file
references. The tool creates native image content without a browser, temporary
HTTP server, path-to-image inference or Base64 in ordinary result JSON.

entries.title: AI tool runtime
entries.description: Canonical navigation and ownership boundary for Redeven AI tools and Floret runtime integration.
entries.summary: Redeven exposes typed AI tools through product-owned registration, policy, presentation, and concrete execution adapters while Floret owns admitted conversation, turn, invocation, approval, and projection lifecycle. This overview is the canonical navigation point for the focused tool, terminal, model/context, thread, and subagent contracts. Detailed behavior belongs in those concepts rather than one cross-domain implementation inventory.

entries.title: Flower storage ownership and migrations
entries.description: Keep canonical Floret storage opaque and preserve every supported product migration through deterministic imports.
entries.summary:
- Authority: Floret owns canonical Agent data and its physical and logical formats; Redeven owns product facts, read state and uploaded resources.
- Outcome: supported existing data upgrades automatically and remains usable for new conversations.
- Invariants: stable database kinds, contiguous transactional migrations, immutable historical decoders, public Floret APIs and one service generation.
- Failure boundary: unknown formats, future versions, drift or failed validation block Flower without resetting data or disabling the core Runtime.

entries.title: Flower backup and recovery
entries.description: Restore preserved Flower collections without replaying old work or backing up every upgrade.
entries.summary:
- Authority: the readiness controller drains generations; each storage owner snapshots and migrates its own data; Floret alone terminates old execution.
- Outcome: administrators can recover Flower history, settings, read state and uploads while other Runtime surfaces remain usable.
- Invariants: no Flower writer during capture or replacement, complete verified collections, preservation of all existing snapshots, and no automatic execution replay.
- Failure boundary: insufficient space, malformed backups, migration defects or interrupted replacement block Flower and preserve recoverable data; recovery does not roll back external actions or binaries.

entries.title: Flower historical writer acceptance
entries.description: Verify every immutable distributed-writer fixture through actual product upgrade and continuation.
entries.summary:
- Authority: locked Redeven writers with released Floret dependencies produce fixture bytes; current tests only copy them.
- Outcome: supported historical data upgrades, remains inspectable and can continue a new conversation.
- Invariants: immutable originals, exact source/module identities, digest verification, product write paths and complete final-main acceptance.
- Failure boundary: fixture drift or a failed upgrade blocks integration; a successful database open alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: Flower attachment resources
entries.description: Owner-scoped uploads, canonical membership, provider reads, quotas, and last-reference cleanup.
entries.summary:
- Authority: Redeven owns attachment bytes, metadata, owner scope, quota, and retention claims; Floret owns the canonical turn and attachment membership.
- Outcome: clients upload bytes once and send opaque `attachment_id` values, while Flower displays an `attachment://v1/...` locator and providers receive only revalidated canonical resources.
- Invariants: physical paths never leave the service, user ownership comes only from the authenticated session, and a product claim never substitutes for an exact Floret membership read.
- Failure boundary: owner mismatch, unsupported media, quota exhaustion, missing canonical membership, metadata drift, digest drift, or missing bytes fails closed without weakening another reference.

entries.title: AI tool permissions and dispatch
entries.description: Tool registration, scheduling, permission, readonly, and target-routing contracts.
entries.summary: Redeven owns product visibility, presentation, current permission policy, prompt, and approval UX; Floret owns invocation and product-neutral tool implementations. Saved thread permission applies at the next authorization boundary within the same task, including queued work, continuation, retry and restart. Each prepared invocation keeps its own snapshot through approval and execution. Missing or invalid authority fails closed. Ordinary calls in one model response enter authorization together and may execute concurrently; dependent work waits for a later response.

entries.title: Computer and browser use runtime
entries.description: Keep target execution, authorization and observation under one Runtime owner while composing semantic actions in bounded scripts.
entries.summary:
`ComputerUseRuntime` owns targets, adapter resources, active control and script
processes. Published Floret owns Agent lifecycle, tool effects and canonical
results. Flower prefers authorized commands and integrations for data work,
semantic browser or desktop operations for interaction, and explicit images for
visual decisions. A missing target, permission or capability fails explicitly;
no adapter silently selects another tab, window or device.

entries.title: Computer semantic snapshots
entries.description: Normalize browser, AX and AT-SPI facts into bounded, revision-scoped semantic trees at the Runtime boundary.
entries.summary:
ComputerUseRuntime owns the model-visible semantic schema, version 2. Browser,
macOS AX and Linux AT-SPI collect native facts; Runtime validates and normalizes
one bounded tree. Relationships never point outside that tree. Unsupported
facts stay absent. Invalid protocol, protected fields or inconsistent graphs
produce a closed observation failure, discard content and preserve confirmed
input effects without replay. Existing target authority and privacy scans remain
mandatory; semantic metadata does not grant input or capture permission.

entries.title: Computer script execution and semantic observations
entries.description: Execute bounded JavaScript against one authorized target without exposing host capabilities or replaying partial effects.
entries.summary:
One `computer.exec` is one Floret tool invocation and one effect attempt.
`ComputerUseRuntime` owns its isolated QuickJS process and checks every host
operation. The guest receives only the controlled `ui`, `browser` and `log`
interfaces. Partial progress survives failure; uncertain effects never replay.
A page change ends the batch with successful partial progress for the Agent.
A permission requirement or private input ends it through Floret's existing
interaction boundary.

entries.title: Optional built-in browser installation
entries.description: Confirm browser acquisition, persist the environment capability switch, and keep setup separate from canonical Flower questions.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns one optional Chromium installation per Runtime state directory.
The capability is enabled by default, but discovery, opening settings, enabling,
and agent tool execution never download bytes. Only an authenticated user's
explicit confirmation starts environment download or automatic Desktop acquisition and upload.
Disabling persists, cancels installation, closes managed browser processes and
blocks further use and installation prompts. Installed bytes and website data
remain. Floret owns the input wait and continuation; installer status never
becomes a second conversation lifecycle. Failed verification never publishes a
partial package, and failures offer an explicit retry or alternative source.

entries.title: Built-in browser Linux system preparation
entries.description: Authorize exact versioned AppArmor preparation without weakening the browser sandbox.
entries.summary:
- Authority: the browser installation manager owns package and launch readiness; a short-lived Runtime command performs the explicitly authorized system transaction.
- Outcome: Ubuntu user-namespace restrictions produce an actionable preparation step, and normal opens reuse the prepared version without repeated authorization.
- Invariants: keep Chromium sandboxing and global AppArmor settings; only compiled catalog bytes may occupy a fixed, root-owned system path; no credentials cross the business API.
- Failure boundary: missing dependencies, unavailable sandbox and unknown launch failures stay distinct; cancelled or failed publication cannot claim readiness or replace saved browser data.

entries.title: Browser and desktop settings
entries.description: Separate environment capability, Chrome pairing, conversation target selection, and grants in one shared settings surface.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns one Browser and desktop dialog shared by Desktop and Env App.
ComputerUseRuntime supplies current host capability and resource discovery;
existing thread settings own selection and access grants; the Chrome extension
owns confirmed pairing consent. These facts never substitute for one another.
Opening, refreshing, or leaving settings never selects a page, grants access,
starts a task, installs components, or launches a private desktop. Failed reads
remain unknown, and a lost selected object remains unavailable until recovered
or explicitly replaced. Floret remains the sole conversation lifecycle owner.

entries.title: Guided personal browser connection
entries.description: Prepare, install and confirm a same-host browser connection without exposing native-host configuration.
entries.summary:
Desktop and Env App share one personal browser connection guide. ComputerUseRuntime owns
connections; Floret ask_user and Respond remain the conversation owners.
The guide is bounded UI observation, not a second execution lifecycle. Users confirm installation and the first connection in Chrome; that profile then restores the same environment connection after restarts. Routine tasks reuse the verified connection without manually selecting a target.

entries.title: Chrome connection diagnostics and recovery
entries.description: Identify Chrome prerequisites, preserve connection failures, and guide recovery on the actual environment host.
entries.summary:
ComputerUseRuntime owns Chrome readiness and its live handshake inventory.
Desktop and Env App present the same host-specific prerequisite and failure
facts. Installed Chrome alone does not establish browser-control readiness.
Missing resources, unavailable graphical sessions, application launch failures,
status-read failures and conversation-continuation failures have separate recovery
instructions. Neither a successful launch nor installation acknowledgement resumes
a task; only a compatible live profile can reach the existing Floret Respond path.
Failures preserve user guidance and never substitute a different browser.

entries.title: Managed browsers and authorized Chrome tabs
entries.description: Bind an explicit profile and tab to the Runtime while preserving login state and unrelated user browsing.
entries.summary:
`ComputerUseRuntime` owns browser connections, authorization and target control.
Managed Chromium, explicit CDP and Chrome extension bindings share the same
restricted page executor. A selected tab never implies authority over sibling
tabs or a different device. Disconnect, revocation, closed tabs and uncertain
effects stop subsequent work without automatically selecting a replacement.

entries.title: Semantic desktop operations and explicit control
entries.description: Use macOS window Accessibility and private Linux AT-SPI before image input while preserving user control.
entries.summary:
`ComputerUseRuntime` owns desktop target execution. macOS targets an explicit
application window; Linux owns a private Xvfb and D-Bus session. Semantic actions
use native accessibility first. A foreground operation requires current task
authorization and respects explicit Stop and takeover. Platform permissions do not prove
that every application or action can run unobtrusively in the background.

entries.title: Computer target selection across threads
entries.description: Resolve logical targets without side effects and preserve each authorized thread selection across turns and restart.
entries.summary:
The Computer Use Runtime owns discovery and selection over Redeven product
settings. Users describe work; Flower finds the browser page or application
window. The current selection is a working position, not a requirement to bind
resources in settings. Candidates never grant access. Stale, disconnected or
occupied resources fail explicitly without changing the previous selection.

entries.title: Computer use safety pauses and user control
entries.description: Separate operation facts from independent Agent questions and require fresh observation before further input.
entries.summary:
Floret owns questions, answers, cancellation and continuation. Redeven owns
computer execution, authorization, private input and media. Operations return
facts or errors; Flower decides whether to call `ask_user` separately. A blocked
capture is never a successful screenshot. Answers reach the Agent unchanged and
do not grant permission, clear safety or replay an operation. Fresh safe
observation is required before further actions. No host waiting table, recovery
journal or second conversation lifecycle exists.

entries.title: Private browser observation and input
entries.description: Fence secret-surface observation, private frames, ordered input and recovery checks around a canonical interaction.
entries.summary:
Runtime owns observer-bound private input and pixels; Floret owns the unresolved
interaction and continuation through the [takeover contract](computer-use-takeover.md).
The user can finish a secret or verification step without exposing its content
to model history. Every operation binds the current observer, viewer revision,
thread, run and target. Unknown input outcomes never replay. Disconnect disables
input immediately; after the canonical answer, Flower resumes in a new Run and
judges the current page through a fresh observation. Private input resumes only
after a newly decoded frame matches the current observer, interaction and target.

entries.title: Computer use media and visual requests
entries.description: Resolve authenticated keyframes and bounded live samples into decoded Flower pixels without persisting image bytes in model history.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns screenshot bytes and authorized media resolution; Floret owns opaque
attachment history and provider rendering. Flower displays saved screenshots inline and offers decoded pixels in a
media-only Stage. Durable keyframes and ephemeral viewing samples have distinct
lifetimes. A missing, changed or unauthorized reference fails explicitly and
cannot fall back to an unrestricted image URL. Successful tool metadata alone
does not prove the user can see a frame.

Durable keyframes share one byte store and canonical retention entry point with
[direct image reads](image-read-and-retention.md). Existing `computer://`
references and their physical root remain unchanged. The media resolver owns
membership authorization without a preceding product detail load.

entries.title: Flower computer viewer presentation
entries.description: Present decoded computer frames with shared window geometry, accessible status and explicit recovery.
entries.summary:
Published Floe owns Stage window geometry and launcher interaction; Flower owns
canonical visual status and presentation scope. Users can view decoded pixels,
move or restore the Stage, and retain geometry across visibility changes. Opening
and closing affect viewing only, never target or execution authority. Missing,
interrupted or private frames retain explicit recovery and cannot borrow an
unrelated public image. Media authorization and sampling remain with the
[Computer use media contract](../ai/computer-use-media.md).

entries.title: Computer use product qualification
entries.description: Establish scope-specific evidence for decoded frames, real target input, control handback and isolated cleanup.
entries.summary:
Redeven qualifies Computer use through the actual product renderer, Runtime,
media decoder and target adapter. A passing scenario proves only its declared
target and provider scope. Fixture outcomes, decoded pixels and cleanup are
required evidence; successful HTTP responses or tool metadata alone are
insufficient. Failed input and uncertain effects must never be replayed to
manufacture a passing result.

entries.title: Computer use qualification evidence
entries.description: Read measured browser and desktop outcomes without conflating adapter, model and final integration scopes.
entries.summary:
The production qualification runners establish scope-specific outcomes under
[the acceptance contract](computer-use-qualification.md). The following results
were observed on 2026-09-17. A passing worktree run does not replace the exact-main
pre-push gate, certify arbitrary applications, or turn earlier failed runs into
successes. Private text and pixels are excluded from retained diagnostics.

entries.title: Computer use paired model measurements
entries.description: Compare visual primitives and semantic scripts through the production Service and report incomplete or failed evidence explicitly.
entries.summary:
Computer use performance is qualified through the production Flower Service,
published Floret, model adapter and managed browser. Paired fixtures measure the
same task with visual primitives and with semantic scripts available. The report
must retain failures and reject missing, duplicate or unmeasured samples.
Headless performance evidence does not establish native desktop or Chrome focus
behavior; those remain separate [acceptance requirements](computer-use-qualification.md).

entries.title: Codex computer and browser use design evidence
entries.description: Separate official guidance and observed packaged behavior from Flower decisions and unresolved platform limits.
entries.summary:
Flower borrows observable design principles, not private implementation code.
Official documentation and read-only inspection of installed app 26.908.40834
and Chrome extension 1.26.901.11451 support command-first routing, persistent
script batches, AX-first interaction, compact observations and independent
visibility/control. They do not establish a universal guarantee that arbitrary
external browser pages can never activate another window. Flower's Runtime
remains the sole execution and authorization owner.

entries.title: AI tool approval and interaction runtime
entries.description: Floret v7 pending interactions, effect authorization, and Flower row-local outcomes.
entries.summary: Pending approval and user input are typed Floret thread interactions. Redeven authorizes the product request and maps safe presentation; it does not persist or recover a second approval lifecycle. Resolve commits the canonical interaction-result batch before updating and publishing the current view. Floret v7.26.0 publishes the unresolved interaction and its matching active projection in one transition: waiting interactions clear `run_progress`, while other active summaries retain it. Redeven therefore never receives an active summary with an invalid combination. Persistence failure returns an error and leaves the live interaction unresolved. Rejection and cancellation are row-local outcomes, never global message failures.

entries.title: AI terminal tool runtime
entries.description: Redeven PTY resources with Floret v7 canonical effect and Activity ownership.
entries.summary: Redeven owns PTY process resources and bounded output retention. Floret v7 owns the canonical tool call, interaction, effect attempt, result, and Activity. One effect adapter authorizes execution once and publishes stable current-view updates; Redeven does not persist a parallel terminal lifecycle or recover effects from product SQL.

entries.title: Model reasoning capabilities and transport
entries.description: Discover verified reasoning controls, preserve explicit intent, and map thinking output and history to provider protocols.
entries.summary:
Published Floret owns the portable reasoning selection contract, Ollama metadata
parser, and Ollama wire encoding. Redeven maps model metadata, product settings,
and provider requests to that contract. Only verified capabilities create
controls; Default, Off, On, named effort, and token budget retain distinct
meanings. Invalid selections fail before provider dispatch, while unknown
controls retain the model's default behavior. Active Turns keep immutable
settings through continuation and restart.

entries.title: Flower prompt and rule sources
entries.description: Keep one Flower introduction separate from runtime facts, capabilities and native engine guidance.
entries.summary:
Flower's host-owned base system prompt contains only its English introduction as
Redeven's general assistant. Every run profile uses the same introduction.
Runtime facts, tool definitions and native Floret guidance retain their own owners
and remain available independently of the product identity.

entries.title: AI model and context runtime
entries.description: Model-source ownership, provider mapping, token limits, context usage, and compaction contracts.
entries.summary: Redeven persists product model and reasoning preferences, provider credentials, and model-source selection, while Floret owns provider-visible context and opaque continuation state. Environment and Desktop model sources remain distinct, context and compaction presentation come from typed Floret observations, and input/output token limits preserve their separate meanings. Product configuration updates merge permission and model state without overwriting unrelated settings.

entries.title: Model provider surface and history
entries.description: Keep provider-visible model history, tool surface refresh, and render lineage under Floret ownership.
entries.summary: Floret owns the provider-visible history and render lineage for each Turn. Redeven supplies the current model surface, prompt, permission snapshot, and ephemeral overlays at the declared boundaries. Historical tool facts remain readable without reintroducing removed tools or rewriting canonical history; provider-surface changes create a new compatible lineage and never become a second continuation store.

entries.title: Model request recovery
entries.description: Recover frozen provider requests through one Engine budget and expose sanitized attempt progress without adding a product lifecycle.
entries.summary: Floret owns retry admission, physical-request deadlines and attempt identity. Redeven supplies protocol facts through one adapter and displays the authoritative current view. Frozen input, confirmed tool exchanges and user cancellation retain their existing authority across transport recovery.

entries.title: Model request measurement
entries.description: Map request-bound native measurement evidence while Floret owns compaction pressure and recovery.
entries.summary: Published Floret v7.70.0 owns one pressure calculation: a qualified native prefix plus an estimate of only the remaining frozen input, or the complete estimate when proof does not match. Redeven supplies protocol facts through optional public contracts.

entries.title: Model request reuse
entries.description: Execute Engine-owned prompt-cache and continuation decisions without creating another history or retry owner.
entries.summary: Floret owns effective reuse decisions and canonical state. Redeven executes them through one prepared request and one Responses consumer. In-memory connections can optimize transmission only after the next canonical state and complete input agree. Failures return to normal turn recovery; supplemental context cannot enable reuse.

entries.title: Flower context compaction and Goal continuation
entries.description: Explicit compaction intent, one upstream execution owner, and recoverable interaction.
entries.summary:
Published Floret v7.74.0 owns compaction admission, installation, Goal continuation,
Stop, Retry and restart. Redeven authorizes and transmits the frozen intent and
presents canonical state. Pure compaction ends after installation or noop; Goal
continuation prepares context and continues work through the existing Engine and
current Goal review in the same execution.

entries.title: Model context usage and compaction
entries.description: Canonical compaction evidence, context usage, and timeline presentation.
entries.summary:
Published Floret owns canonical context, compaction and usage. Redeven presents
its typed snapshots without accumulating usage or reconstructing lifecycle facts.
[Context compaction and Goal continuation](flower-context-compaction.md) defines
manual intent, admission, execution, cancellation and recovery. [Qualification](../operations/flower-compaction-qualification.md) defines deterministic, historical-copy and real-provider checks.

entries.title: Flower context compaction qualification
entries.description: Isolated deterministic, historical-copy, and real-provider compaction acceptance.
entries.summary:
Compaction qualification uses isolated state and explicit test lanes. Production
threads are never continued by historical-copy inspection. The [execution contract](../ai/flower-context-compaction.md) owns intent and recovery; [usage presentation](../ai/model-context-usage-and-compaction.md) maps canonical observations.

entries.title: Flower Ollama context qualification
entries.description: Exercise the selected installed model through Flower and compare compaction, native token usage, live observations, and restart recovery.
entries.summary:
The opt-in Ollama qualification uses the production Flower service, its model
gateway, and the published Floret thread runtime. Native provider usage must
agree with canonical Flower context and cumulative totals; compaction must
preserve facts through a real model-generated checkpoint and restart. Tests own
their temporary state and loopback recording proxy. A provider or assertion
failure fails the run; it never substitutes a simulated response or changes the
user's model configuration.

entries.title: Flower context distribution qualification
entries.description: Historical token attribution evidence and current native-token plus visible-character qualification.
entries.summary:
Current presentation uses published Floret v7.60.3: native input tokens and
same-request visible Unicode characters are independent facts. Historical token
comparison and remainder results below are retained as evidence, not current
product behavior or proof of complete OpenAI attribution. The current contract
is [Presentation](../ai/flower-managed-model-context.md#presentation).

entries.title: Flower Ollama task qualification
entries.description: Run real selected-model tasks through production Flower commands and verify effects, interruption, recovery, and subagent handoffs.
entries.summary:
The opt-in task qualification calls the selected installed Ollama model through
the production Flower service and published Floret runtime. The model chooses
real tool calls; assertions inspect actual files, terminal processes, canonical
views, and the workspace stream. A failed scenario remains a failure, with no
simulated replacement or automatic rerun. Tests own isolated state and stop only
their own services and tools. Source configuration and credentials stay unchanged.

entries.title: DeepSeek Responses
entries.description: Flower consumes Floret stateless Responses transport with explicit web tool limits.
entries.summary:
Flower routes the DeepSeek provider to the published Floret v7.66.1 Responses gateway.
Floret owns `/responses` rendering, SSE parsing, reasoning, usage normalization,
function-call validation, and opaque provider history. Redeven only maps its
model DTOs and canonical dotted tool names to provider-safe aliases.

entries.title: Flower canonical thread queries
entries.description: Authorize canonical active-path search, counts and bounded content reads through released Floret tools.
entries.summary:
Floret v7.32.0 owns the canonical journal and its derived in-memory index.
Redeven exposes `threads.query`, `threads.read` and `threads.aggregate` as
read-only mappings to optional `runtime.ThreadQueryReader`. Every invocation
rebuilds the current readable scope before search, sorting, counting or reading.
References never grant access. Expired or invalidated cursors fail explicitly;
the model can narrow its query or start again.

entries.title: Floret thread runtime integration
entries.description: Typed Floret v7 thread runtime ownership and Redeven product boundaries.
entries.summary: Floret v7 `ThreadService` is the sole owner of active and canonical thread lifecycle. Redeven owns endpoint authorization, attachment resource resolution, provider and tool effects, and browser-safe mapping. Every existing-thread mutation proves that the ThreadID belongs to the authenticated endpoint before entering Floret. Send, Respond, Cancel, Retry, and the optional independent CompactContext return the current typed view without waiting for provider continuation. Canonical journal facts prevent duplicate user, assistant, tool, and interaction records; transient drafts and execution tokens remain in memory.

entries.title: Floret Redeven adapter and projection
entries.description: Map authorized Redeven requests and Floret typed views without creating a second thread lifecycle.
entries.summary: Redeven's adapter is a thin typed boundary over published Floret. It authorizes endpoint and thread ownership, resolves resources, sanitizes Activity, maps typed views, native updates and failures, and projects live summaries. Floret remains the only lifecycle, persistence, migration, cancellation, and provider-state owner; Redeven never waits on provider work or mirrors a receipt, authority barrier, transcript, or execution projection.

entries.title: Flower subagent parent events
entries.description: Canonical parent reports, passive lifecycle events, and bounded waiting.
entries.summary: SubAgent reports and lifecycle events remain canonical Floret facts, visible to the direct parent without creating another handoff store. They do not wake idle parents; bounded waiting and explicit reads expose reports when the parent continues. Tool approval and user input remain ordinary child interactions, while questions and blockers can be reported through `report_to_parent` without ending the delegated task.

entries.title: Flower subagent runtime
entries.description: Canonical child threads, direct task instructions, scoped reads, and complete handoffs.
entries.summary: Floret v7 owns each SubAgent as a normal canonical child Thread. Redeven exposes product tools and Flower mappings over the typed `ThreadRuntime` without a second child identity, result store, recovery projection, or child lifecycle table. Parent-scoped summaries are bounded status only; the canonical child current view is the only complete handoff authority.

entries.title: Flower thread fork coordination
entries.description: Redeven authorizes a source thread, selects a full-thread or answer-anchored Floret fork, and adopts settings for the canonical destination.
entries.summary:
- Authority: Floret owns the forked journal and canonical destination identity; Redeven owns endpoint authorization and the destination's product settings.
- Outcome: one stable client request forks the authorized source, adopts settings for the returned destination, and optionally sets an explicit title.
- Invariants: source ownership is proven before Floret mutation, the returned destination is the only product adoption target, and the product stores no fork receipt, saga, or canonical lifecycle copy.
- Failure boundary: invalid request identity, foreign source authority, Floret failure, or conflicting destination settings fails explicitly without a recovery coordinator or compensating canonical delete.

entries.title: Flower thread deletion coordination
entries.description: Synchronous, idempotent convergence across Floret canonical deletion and Redeven product cleanup.
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical thread deletion and Redeven owns product settings, read state, execution authority, and attachment claims. One authenticated DELETE request performs those two owner operations in that order and returns success only after both complete. The operation is synchronous, idempotent, and retryable; it does not claim cross-database atomicity or persist a second lifecycle receipt.

entries.title: Flower plugin generation
entries.description: Flower-generated plugins are Redeven product orchestration through Floret and released ReDevPlugin lifecycle APIs.
entries.summary:
Flower can help users create plugins, but the generated-plugin flow is not a
second plugin platform. Redeven owns the user intent capture, prompt
orchestration, review UX, approval presentation, and product timeline
projection. ReDevPlugin owns templates, validators, package builders, lifecycle
APIs, runtime contracts, sandbox surfaces, and platform policy. Floret owns the
tool dispatch and approval lifecycle that Flower must use.

entries.title: Flower context action admission
entries.description: Ask Flower context actions become Floret-owned message references and durable model-context snapshots at admission.
entries.summary:
- Authority: Redeven owns a user-selected context action only before admission; Floret owns the admitted user message, ordered references, and Agent context lifecycle.
- Outcome: one admission mapper validates and authorizes the submitted context action, then produces ordered durable `MessageReference` values and durable `UserInput.Context` snapshots.
- Invariants: Redeven does not persist the mapped references, runtime context, or a post-admission context-action copy.
- Failure boundary: malformed envelopes, unknown kinds, privacy-matrix violations, forged resource targets, and projection failures reject admission; the launcher preserves editable draft text and references.

entries.title: Redeven environment operations
entries.description: redeven env and redeven targets exec are the product boundaries for Flower and automation environment lifecycle and target diagnostic requests.
entries.summary: Redeven environment lifecycle requests must go through the Redeven product surface, not through inferred container, SSH, systemd, launchctl, or process-manager commands. Flower learns this boundary through the standard `redeven-environment` system skill, not through a bespoke environment workflow embedded in the global prompt.

entries.title: OKF bundle lifecycle
entries.description: Redeven builds a deterministic embedded OKF bundle from source Markdown concepts.
entries.summary: Redeven builds its embedded OKF bundle from curated source files under the top-level `okf/` authoring root, verifies deterministic dist outputs under `okf/dist/`, and embeds the resulting bundle into the binary used by Runtime and AI features for local retrieval.

entries.title: OKF tool suite
entries.description: OKF tools expose read-only Redeven repository knowledge through index browsing, short search, and concept opening.
entries.summary: Redeven exposes the embedded OKF bundle through read-only `okf.index`, `okf.search`, and `okf.open` builtin tools. Redeven projects bounded safe results into Floret v7.26.0 structured Activity rows, and the shared Flower surface expands those rows without reading raw OKF result JSON.

entries.title: Gateway v6 protocol
entries.description: Define signed pairing, member invitations, policy, reverse access and versioned Cloud association.
entries.summary: `redeven-gateway-v6` is the only served Gateway membership protocol. Its machine-readable authority is `spec/openapi/gateway-v6.yaml`. A signed invitation-code delivery carries administrator-confirmed share addresses. The authenticated exchange returns the signed internal enrollment descriptor with all confirmed Runtime connection endpoints. Gateway owns paired Desktop permissions and Runtime-initiated membership. Protocol mismatch fails explicitly; old URL-profile routes and HTTP forwarding are absent. Old Gateway configuration is rejected read-only; it is never silently rewritten. Gateway Cloud v3 is a separate, shared business contract referring to these same members.

entries.title: RCPP v5 Cloud API
entries.description: Single Cloud input, authoritative Access Point assignment, native OAuth and access authorization.
entries.summary: RCPP v5 separates Cloud authorization from network route. CloudRuntimeBinding owns environment, Runtime identity, Namespace, user or Namespace principal and generation. One Runtime ConnectionController handles direct and Gateway enrollment, registration, heartbeat, reserve maintenance and recovery. Desktop never creates a second credential recovery owner.

entries.title: Self-contained installer distribution
entries.description: Pin a prebuilt installer, authenticate detached release evidence in process, and activate a complete Runtime suite atomically.
entries.summary:
Release packaging builds `redeven-installer_<os>_<arch>` for macOS and Linux,
AMD64 and ARM64, with CGO disabled. It renders `redeven-install.sh` from the
actual four binary digests and signs both the binaries and entry through
`SHA256SUMS`. No receiving-host Go, Cosign, Python, OpenSSL or package manager
is required. A standard shell, HTTPS downloader and SHA-256 utility remain
bootstrap prerequisites.

entries.title: CI and release gates
entries.description: Redeven binds published dependencies, generated assets, UI behavior, release payloads, tests, and OKF to the exact main tip being pushed.
entries.summary:
Redeven uses focused checks during implementation, a fast staged pre-commit
gate, and one complete integration gate for the exact main tip being pushed.
Published dependency evidence, generated assets, localized public docs, UI
behavior, Desktop/runtime bundles, Go tests, lint, and OKF must all agree. A
missing, stale, unsigned, optional, or target-mismatched ReDevPlugin artifact
fails release packaging.
Windows is an internal certification target only; the formal release inventory
fails closed if any Windows asset appears.

entries.title: ReDevPlugin release artifact gate
entries.description: Verify the released ReDevPlugin publication, native runtime evidence, packaging inventory, and exact collector inputs.
entries.summary: Redeven admits only the coordinated ReDevPlugin release published through its exact manifest, registry readbacks, native runtime evidence, and closed installer inventory. Every artifact is bound to the release tag, source commit, target, digest, signature identity, and package receipt before publication; partial, mutable, Windows, or target-mismatched inputs fail closed.

entries.title: Plugin integration gate
entries.description: Qualify released ReDevPlugin Host, market, runtime, and UI integration on the exact main tip.
entries.summary: The plugin integration gate proves that the released ReDevPlugin Host and market contracts remain aligned with Redeven's authorization, placement, renderer, and Desktop lifecycle adapters. It uses the published package and isolated smoke profiles; copied platform paths, implicit grants, second bridges, and stale lifecycle projections fail closed.

entries.title: OKF release assets
entries.description: Release workflow publishes OKF verification assets alongside CLI and desktop artifacts.
entries.summary:
GitHub releases ship `okf_bundle.manifest.json` and `okf_bundle.sha256` together with CLI tarballs, desktop packages, and signed `SHA256SUMS`.

Release workflow publishes OKF verification assets alongside CLI and desktop artifacts.

The signed aggregate checksum remains the public integrity anchor for these standalone verification files.

entries.title: Automated service-template catalog updates
entries.description: Follow verified upstream catalog tags through isolated source updates and the exact-main integration gate.
entries.summary:
The template repository owns recommendation discovery and immutable catalog releases.
Redeven's daily and manually dispatched watcher owns adoption of the published Go
module into source `main`. A successful update pins verified checksums, regenerates
notices and knowledge artifacts, and passes the normal final integration gate.
Failures preserve the last published main tip; a failed or uncertain push requires
remote-ref inspection before another attempt.

entries.title: Flower managed runtime facts
entries.description: One snapshot collector supplies canonical facts through published Floret admission and request boundaries.
entries.summary:
Flower consumes published Floret v7.47.1. One complete collector supplies four
stable partitions: execution environment, date/timezone, repository rule
sources, and available skills. Floret owns chronological admission,
semantic changes, user-role model-context messages, compaction and recovery.
The product owns collection and authorized presentation only.

concepts.summary: Redeven exposes typed AI tools through product-owned registration, policy, presentation, and concrete execution adapters while Floret owns admitted conversation, turn, invocation, approval, and projection lifecycle. This overview is the canonical navigation point for the focused tool, terminal, model/context, thread, and subagent contracts. Detailed behavior belongs in those concepts rather than one cross-domain implementation inventory.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
This concept is the stable overview for the subject.

Floret renders reference display content and snapshots into canonical model history for execution and compaction, preserving order across follow-ups.

Lease release follows the canonical terminal view, not the HTTP response or Desktop connection lifetime, so an existing session cannot admit hidden work after the final lifecycle snapshot.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Redeven must consume published Floret releases and must not persist a second copy of Floret-owned conversation, tool, approval, todo, context, projection, or provider state. Tool and execution provenance must come from explicit contracts and results rather than inference.

concepts.title: ChatGPT account lifecycle
concepts.description: Persist verified local sign-ins, reuse issued registrations and complete renewal, cancellation and logout independently of connection editing.

frontmatter.description: Persist verified local sign-ins, reuse issued registrations and complete renewal, cancellation and logout independently of connection editing.
frontmatter.title: ChatGPT account lifecycle

concepts.summary:
Redeven's canonical protected account store owns verified ChatGPT registrations
and sessions. Returning setup reuses saved registrations; only explicit new-account
or workspace intent creates another. Email is never a registration or workspace
key. OAuth completion persists sign-in independently of connection
editing; identity-only grants never admit inference. Retry reuses issued client
identity with fresh OAuth inputs. Renewal and logout serialize rotating tokens.
Cancellation never installs usable credentials after its commit boundary, and
interrupted cleanup uses the existing durable logout journal. Storage failure
stops account use; local cleanup and remote revocation remain separate outcomes.
Local admission is owned by the [authentication contract](chatgpt-local-authentication.md).

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Sign-in and registration
One `chatgpt.Client` owns bounded, five-minute in-memory attempts.

Interrupted logout is completed at startup; normal maintenance scans never clear a live logout.

## Renewal and credential coordination
[Account maintenance](../../internal/chatgpt/lifecycle.go) starts with the Runtime service, independently of AI readiness, connection bindings and open windows. Runtime shutdown cancels maintenance without signing out and never schedules OS background work.

Account updates use model_directory.changed and merge independently of drafts.

## Logout and connection changes
Sign-out first records intent and stops related tasks through Floret's existing immediate Cancel with descendants. The private Desktop model source observes current account facts once per second and passes confirmed account stop reasons to its owning Runtime; it never owns another task lifecycle.

The Runtime Service protocol, secrets schema, Floret public API and domain migration remain unchanged.

concepts.summary:

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Connecting an explicitly chosen tab or creating a new tab in Browser and desktop also selects that target for the current conversation. Approval Required uses the current target and URL through tool approval; temporary URL authorization never becomes a saved origin grant.

It is not a model tool or a second browser-opening path.

## Managed profiles
Both Flower carriers use the shared browser installation controller at `/_redeven_proxy/api/browser/installation`.

The default profile creates its first page lazily; later loss of a selected page fails explicitly.

The guest cannot choose filesystem destinations or read file bytes; a later authorized file/command tool handles data processing.

## Chrome extension and explicit CDP
The MV3 extension uses Native Messaging and `chrome.debugger` bound to an exact tab.

Its webNavigation creation events retain bounded, in-memory popup source facts; Chrome tab-group opener metadata is not treated as the source of an action.

A remote Linux task uses its remote managed browser or private desktop; it cannot silently drive local user Chrome.

sections.title: Boundaries

See the [Codex design evidence](computer-use-design-evidence.md) for the public and installed-code comparison; no forced reload or CSP rewriting is used.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Result encoding recovery
Run the explicit local browser qualification from the repository root:

It builds the production FlowerSurface with installed published UI packages, uses the production runtime adapter and canonical detail projection against a real task-owned Service, and injects one counted executor effect followed by an invalid optional result. It is opt-in and stays outside ordinary CI and exact-main gates.

## Semantic execution acceptance
Browser and desktop belong to one delivery scope.

Cancellation and revocation before the click prevent dispatch; unknown click acknowledgements remain terminal.

Foreground macOS and credentialed model qualification remain explicit runs; the integration gate cannot substitute for their evidence.

## Existing product fixtures
Desktop qualification observes the preload workspace stream; Linux Webtop uses CDP's passive HTTP workspace stream copy. A missing native or browser live-frame match fails that scope.

Independent questions retain their generated question IDs, choices and text editor. A failed setup panel allows retry, close and ordinary answering or Stop; changing conversations always remains possible.

These process-local controls do not become durable Floret state.

## Model output and presentation
[tool_result_encoding.go](../../internal/ai/tool_result_encoding.go) owns the single final result encoder: execution facts, tool content policy, final JSON, then Text and an independent Decoder.UseNumber Structured snapshot. Activity independently projects valid source data; its display truncation never changes model output.

Its `request_key` remains the send idempotency identity used only to settle the short-lived browser outbox; the two values are not interchangeable.

Flower ask_user exposes only write and select_or_write. The latter always presents fixed choices with a separate custom-text answer, even when write_label is omitted. Floret owns normalization of historical select requests; Redeven does not add a second compatibility path. Ordinary InputRequired selection remains a separate contract.

Ordinary startup, binary changes and transactional migrations do not create full snapshots. A damaged old snapshot cannot block healthy live data.

Abandoned task staging is removed only after any durable replacement completes and before a new generation opens; an unclosed generation prevents that path.
