Settings and the Flower maintenance action expose backup time, source build, size and protection.

Old unfinished Turns become terminal, old interactions become resolved and non-executable, and queued input remains canonical readonly `RestoredInputs`.

Diagnostics use the existing sanitized export and do not include conversations, credentials, database contents or uploaded files by default.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Compaction and continuation
[Manual compaction](flower-context-compaction.md) defaults to explicit continue_goal intent. Retry and restart use canonical preparation and confirmed tools. Redeven forwards intent and renders state without a second execution coordinator.

## Goal ownership and execution
User and model updates enter Floret's shared journal writer with request identity and expected version. An existing unfinished Goal remains authoritative across continuation and context restoration.

Stop cancels execution and reflection; deletion only cancels future Goal checks.

## Interaction and recovery
Selecting or entering /goal opens an in-composer command chip.

Each popup opening confirms detail through the existing read coordinator before showing canonical text.

A failed binding leaves the draft available for retry; no cross-thread target validation is relaxed and no attachment is uploaded twice.

sections.body:

Default Flower tools, capability lists and prompts omit write_todos and current Todo state. Deleting Todo later requires no change to Goal execution or interaction.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
[Goal changes](flower-goals.md) use Floret-owned typed context facts, separate from the four product-collected partitions.

Skill rediscovery uses one authoritative catalog and deterministic text; disabled or newly restricted skills cannot reuse an activation cache. Loaded skill instructions remain historical model facts.

## Skill catalog and explicit reads
The automatic skill catalog contains current available names and descriptions in stable priority/name order.

Disabled, deleted, restricted, unreadable or invalid skills cannot return older instructions as current content.

Whole-request wire bytes and body tool-result bytes are reported separately by the regression tests; these are byte measurements, not tokenizer counts or production change rates.

## Snapshot lifecycle
UserInput.Context retains ordinary submitted facts and references. Automatic facts use ModelContextSnapshot, never historical free-text parsing.

No new thread, storage migration, historical text parsing, or product-owned snapshot is required.

Authorized canonical reads and the existing workspace subscription carry the same snapshot, record location, changed/removed keys and latest request use.

Subtask details use the same component and bounded detail cache.

## Presentation
One confirmed request supplies native input-token usage, visible Unicode character counts and recent cache rate as independent measurements. Missing historical values remain unavailable; visible characters never estimate or explain token differences, and no provider history is reconstructed.

frontmatter.title: Flower plugin generation

concepts.summary:
Flower can help users create plugins, but the generated-plugin flow is not a
second plugin platform. Redeven owns the user intent capture, prompt
orchestration, review UX, approval presentation, and product timeline
projection. ReDevPlugin owns templates, validators, package builders, lifecycle
APIs, runtime contracts, sandbox surfaces, and platform policy. Floret owns the
tool dispatch and approval lifecycle that Flower must use.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
A Flower-generated plugin flow is a sequence of approved product actions over released ReDevPlugin APIs.

A plugin-generation handler may run already-approved local steps and call released ReDevPlugin adapters, but it must not perform its own approval wait, bypass Floret dispatch, mutate Flower activity rows directly, or convert plugin audit rows into Flower timeline state.

If a generated plugin needs a platform capability that does not exist in released ReDevPlugin, the requirement is recorded upstream instead of hidden behind a Redeven-local helper.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Flower must not write plugin registry rows, mint bridge tokens, place plugin UI assets directly under Env App routes, bypass package inspection, signature assessment, explicit confirmation, or trust policy, grant storage/network/ runtime access outside ReDevPlugin brokers, or call a business adapter before ReDevPlugin has built the request context.

A requested approval remains waiting until Floret resolves it.

concepts.summary:
- Authority: Floret owns canonical Agent data and its physical and logical formats; Redeven owns product facts, read state and uploaded resources.
- Outcome: supported existing data upgrades automatically and remains usable for new conversations.
- Invariants: stable database kinds, contiguous transactional migrations, immutable historical decoders, public Floret APIs and one service generation.
- Failure boundary: unknown formats, future versions, drift or failed validation block Flower without resetting data or disabling the core Runtime.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Storage owners
Redeven consumes published Floret v7.78.2 with `GOWORK=off`.

Ordinary Floret writes stage, validate and persist affected canonical records only; startup, migrations and explicit integrity checks still validate the complete repository.

A read-state failure cannot become a core Runtime constructor failure or a synthetic read record.

## Readonly checks and owner transactions
`sqliteutil` owns WAL-aware readonly preflight, integrity checks and complete SQLite snapshots for product and read-state owners. Inspection never creates missing data or runs a migration.

Required upgrade snapshots precede Floret space maintenance and all migrations, as specified by the [backup and recovery contract](flower-backup-and-recovery.md).

## Frozen historical queue conversion
The migration-only `pendinginputlegacy` package owns the complete interpretation of historical queue bytes: session identity, options, context shapes, default values, resource metadata and normalization limits.

The v4-to-v5 product transaction imports canonical pending inputs through Floret's public idempotent import API, records necessary product authority and removes retired source tables before commit. The upgrade operation contains only target build, original snapshot identity and completion; owner versions and canonical records remain the progress authority.

## Resource and authorization retention
Product upload references retain resources for every canonical thread that contains them, including ordinary forks, nested forks and restored inputs.

Bounded keyset maintenance and compaction stop and drain with their owning generation.

sections.title: Contract

`ForkThreadWithOptions` validates RWX access, the source ThreadID, endpoint identity, and a stable `client_request_id`. The shared endpoint/thread authority boundary must find a live product settings row for that exact endpoint before any Floret call.

An optional `source_item_id` selects a committed assistant answer on the active path. Floret retains that answer and its preceding history while excluding later items. Answer-level Fork supplies this anchor; thread-list Fork omits it and retains the current full path. Invalid or uncommitted anchors fail explicitly.

Detail recovery retains the created destination and retries loading only.

Floret v7.32.0 owns the canonical journal and its derived in-memory index.
Redeven exposes `threads.query`, `threads.read` and `threads.aggregate` as

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Authorization owner
Authenticated session authority supplies read permission, user, endpoint and namespace identity. These fields plus user identity bind the upstream scope; tool schemas cannot accept model-authored authority. Redeven never reads Floret SQL, canonical records or internal packages, and offers no arbitrary SQL tool.

## Query and content boundary
The upstream public `threadquery` types define objects, filters, sorting, aggregation and pagination.

Schema-invalid keys enter its bounded correction path before tool dispatch and do not create visible failed Activity rows.

Historical results remain readable after restart even when original query refs have expired.

## Index and snapshots
The canonical log owner rebuilds its derived index after startup verification and updates it only after successful canonical commits.

A new query uses current authority and never silently expands the old scope.

frontmatter.title: Direct image reading and tool media retention

concepts.summary:
`image.read(file_path, target_id)` reads an image directly in every permission
mode. Its exclusive `locator` mode rereads an admitted immutable snapshot in the
current thread without reopening the original file or copying bytes. Redeven
owns authorization and immutable bytes; Floret owns the typed
attachment, model history and canonical membership. File references stay file
references. The tool creates native image content without a browser, temporary
HTTP server, path-to-image inference or Base64 in ordinary result JSON.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Authorized reads
The shared read-only tool checks model image capability, `CanRead`, filesystem scope and `ToolTargetPolicy`. An explicit unavailable target fails rather than using another device.

Native image budgeting inspects these protocol parts and does not count Base64 transport as ordinary text.

## Visual summaries and rereads
Published Floret v7.51.1 projects user and confirmed tool attachments into one ordered visual compaction input. Full rendered request budgets include image cost; an image that cannot fit fails explicitly.

File reads keep their 10 MiB bound; admitted Computer frames retain their existing 16 MiB bound.

## Immutable bytes and retention
One `toolMediaStore` owns image snapshots and existing Computer keyframes under the original `computer/keyframes` root. Changes or deletion of the source file cannot alter subsequent sends, retry, restart, fork or compaction.

No product or Floret storage schema changes.

## Authorized previews
The resolver is the only membership and endpoint authorization entry point. It reads product thread ownership and one public canonical view, without the full product detail mapper.

Assistant Markdown images retain their existing presentation.

concepts.title: Flower MCP runtime
concepts.description: Configure external MCP servers and execute their tools through Flower's existing Floret authorization boundary.

frontmatter.description: Configure external MCP servers and execute their tools through Flower's existing Floret authorization boundary.
frontmatter.title: Flower MCP runtime

concepts.summary:
Redeven owns administrator-managed MCP configuration and a thin product adapter
over the released official Model Context Protocol Go SDK. The SDK owns stdio
and Streamable HTTP protocol sessions. Floret owns invocation identity,
approval, one-shot effect authorization, history, and recovery through the
[typed thread runtime](floret-thread-runtime.md). MCP must not introduce another
execution queue, lifecycle projection, or retry authority. A lost call outcome
is terminal and cannot be replayed. Invalid persisted configuration fails closed
without changing the original bytes.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Configuration and protocol
Configuration lives at `<stateDir>/ai/mcp.json`, with schema version 2, one monotonic configuration revision, and server revisions for optimistic edits. Persistence failure leaves the in-memory catalog unchanged.

Catalog limits are 32 servers, 128 tools per server, 32 KiB per schema, and 4 MiB total persisted configuration.

## Presentation icons
Save and explicit Check read `serverInfo.icons` from the existing SDK initialize result. Connection-preserving disabled edits retain icons; changed connection settings clear stale discovery.

Rejected sources receive the generated identity described in [the shared UI contract](../ui/flower-extensions.md#entry-icons).

## Execution and dependencies
Enabled, previously discovered tools join the dynamic tool surface before the existing permission filter. Their identity binds the exact server configuration and tool schema, so a changed or disabled configuration cannot execute through an old invocation name.

Enabled, checked configuration satisfies the catalog indicator; it does not promise current network reachability or bypass approval.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
MCP tools are conservatively mutating and open-world regardless of server annotation claims. An MCP handler cannot run directly without that proof.

Server tool errors and known connection failures remain distinct from an unknown execution outcome.

## Request output budgets
Redeven passes model output capability as Floret ModelMaxOutputTokens, and only an explicit per-request limit as MaxOutputTokens. It never maps capability to a fixed output reservation.

The comparison logs are /tmp/redeven-budget-desktop-failures-focused.log and /tmp/redeven-budget-desktop-main-baseline.log.

## Mechanism
Model reasoning capability, stream fields, history replay, and immutable thread settings are governed by [model reasoning capabilities and transport](model-reasoning-runtime.md).

Unsupported transports reject non-empty state before HTTP.

Hosted-turn diagnostics record the selected wire mode, and Floret lifecycle audit events carry batch index, batch size, event type, and observation time so operators can distinguish model serialization, provider single-call output, approval wait, dispatch, and completion without feeding diagnostics back into scheduling.

## Prompt and repository rule sources
[Flower prompt and rule sources](flower-prompt-and-rule-sources.md) owns task, interaction, recovery, complete rule reading, and runtime-context admission policy.

## Related provider history
Provider-visible history, render lineage, and unavailable-tool continuity are owned by [Model provider surface and history](model-provider-surface-and-history.md).

## Related context usage
Usage accounting, context pressure, compaction, token budgets, and capacity failures are owned by [Model context usage and compaction](model-context-usage-and-compaction.md).

concepts.summary:
Published Floret owns canonical context, compaction and usage. Redeven presents
its typed snapshots without accumulating usage or reconstructing lifecycle facts.
[Context compaction and Goal continuation](flower-context-compaction.md) defines
manual intent, admission, execution, cancellation and recovery. [Qualification](../operations/flower-compaction-qualification.md) defines deterministic, historical-copy and real-provider checks.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Compaction decision evidence
The canonical lifecycle optionally retains the frozen trigger candidate, pressure and validated replacement.

Pointer exit, Escape, Tab, focus loss and outside pointer actions dismiss the layer; process collapse closes it through the existing visibility owner.

## Projection and usage
Floret installs the complete context snapshot in its actor-owned current view before publishing its version. Context changes bypass text cadence, while equal snapshots still coalesce text growth within the existing bounded queues.

Redeven does not invent a total budget or infer serving capacity from model weights.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:

Cloud execution consumes its catalog protocol rather than fetching inventory during dispatch.

No Floret schema migration is added.

frontmatter.title: OKF bundle lifecycle

concepts.summary: Redeven builds its embedded OKF bundle from curated source files under the top-level `okf/` authoring root, verifies deterministic dist outputs under `okf/dist/`, and embeds the resulting bundle into the binary used by Runtime and AI features for local retrieval.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
`build_assets.sh` invokes `build_okf_bundle.sh`, which runs `cmd/okf-bundle` against explicit source and dist roots. The builder emits the bundle, manifest and checksum deterministically. Summary and section bodies are embedded as structured data; Evidence remains in its source file but is omitted from ordinary concept opening unless requested. `okf/dist/*` is generated from source and is never an authoring surface.

## Quality gates
Report mode exposes layout, indexing, summary, evidence, duplication, lifecycle and budget issues without blocking cleanup. Strict mode fails structural and source-integrity violations, overdue reviews, and source totals above the hard cap. Final integration runs strict content quality after source integrity and before verifying the generated bundle.

## Source budget
Count Unicode characters in every source Markdown file under `okf/`, including the index and log, after CRLF-to-LF normalization; exclude `okf/dist/`. The report shows total, remaining capacity and index/concept/log usage. Exceeding 900,000 warns; strict quality accepts exactly 1,000,000 and fails above it. A per-concept `quality_exception` cannot waive this hard cap.

## Review and log lifecycle
Every concept declares `lifecycle` and `reviewed_at`: review contracts every 180 days, active measurements and operational evidence every 90 days, and retained history every 365 days. Retained history also needs a concise `retention_reason`. Report mode warns and strict mode fails on invalid or overdue metadata; expiry prompts review and never deletes a document automatically. Keep `log.md` to compact summaries from the last 30 days after durable knowledge moves into its concept.

## Index and retention
Keep categories and concept links in the index; the parser derives each retrieval summary from the concept's `# Summary`. Prefer an existing concept, preserve only decision-relevant historical conclusions and counterevidence, and remove obsolete detail from the current tree so Git history remains the recovery path.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The bundle remains auditable only while OKF Markdown concepts are the sole authoring surface, source and lifecycle budgets are enforced through the shared parser, and `okf/dist/*` stays a generated verification artifact set rather than hand-edited truth. A `quality_exception` may document a justified per-concept length exception, but it never waives the source cap or other quality checks.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
Runtime OKF code loads the embedded bundle once, indexes root directory sections, scores structured summaries and sections in memory, and opens a concept summary or one selected section by id or path. Internal ids, paths, and unfiltered result objects never enter that display contract. OKF activity labels and operation values come from `ToolPresentationSpec`, so the Floret projection does not own a separate OKF display vocabulary.

## Tool workflow
`okf.index` browses `okf/index.md` as a structured directory and returns summaries plus section counts. `okf.search` returns a bounded short candidate list with query-aware snippets and the best matching section id/title; title and Summary matches outrank section body matches.

Models should follow `okf.index -> okf.search -> okf.open Summary -> okf.open section` and must not rely on snippets for detailed contracts.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The tools return scoped Redeven repository knowledge and do not mutate OKF source or dist artifacts. They must not be used for current news, recent public events, market or pricing facts, third-party documentation, external facts, or general web facts. Source-level conclusions still require file or terminal verification after OKF navigation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
The 2026-10-12 review covers all existing provider types. Audio, video, embeddings, and restricted-access specialized models are outside the default Agent directory.

| Provider | Current public Agent models reviewed | Runtime route and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI | GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna | `/v1/responses`; function tools for GPT-6.1 Sol require Responses. Sol/Luna permit `none`; 6.1 Sol and Astra do not. 1,050,000 context and 128,000 output tokens. |
| Anthropic | Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and 4.5 | `/v1/messages`, API version `2023-06-01`; SDK base is the origin without `/v1`. Opus/Sonnet 5.5 use adaptive thinking with effort, reject manual budgets and `disabled`, and expose 1M context / 128K output. |
| Google | Gemini 3.8 Flash | Supported `/v1beta/openai/chat/completions` with model-specific effort/budget settings and opaque tool thought signatures. Existing directory already includes the current model. |
| DeepSeek | `deepseek-flash` (V4.1 Flash), `deepseek-v4-pro` | The published Floret v7.78.2 Responses gateway accepts the new name; the capability was introduced and qualified in v7.19.0. Flash and both official aliases support images, while Pro is text-only. All support off/low/high/max and a 393,216-token output ceiling. Built-in search remains ignored by the provider. |
| Qwen | Qwen3.8 Max, Flash, Omni Flash | `/compatible-mode/v1/chat/completions`; existing qualified search models use Responses. New Omni Flash is text output with tools and text/image input in Redeven. Qwen3.7 Max/Plus output ceilings rise to 131,072. |
| Moonshot | Kimi K3, K2.7 Code, K2.6 | `/v1/chat/completions`; K3 requires thinking, supports low/high/max, and accepts `max_completion_tokens` up to 1,048,576 (provider default 131,072). Search for K3 remains unintegrated. |
| Z.ai | GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash/FlashX | `/api/paas/v4/chat/completions`; FlashX has 1M context and 128K output, forced thinking with low/high/max. The persisted provider type stays `chatglm`; display branding is Z.ai. |
| xAI | Grok 4.7 | Existing `/v1/chat/completions` is still supported but marked legacy. Responses is the supplier's preferred API for new features. 4.7 supports low/medium/high/xhigh, defaults to high, and cannot disable thinking. |
| Groq | GPT-OSS 120B/20B and Qwen3.8-27B | `/openai/v1/chat/completions`; preview status stays explicit. Existing catalog is current. |
| OpenRouter | Dynamic provider inventory | Discover tool-capable models from `/api/v1/models`; preserve explicit user selection. |
| Ollama | Installed local inventory | `/api/tags`, `/api/ps`, `/api/show`, then `/v1/chat/completions`; serving context and tools must be discovered. |
| Custom compatible | User-defined models | Retain explicit endpoint, token limits, and capability configuration. |

The generated catalog must include only models that have a released adapter, a reviewed endpoint and capability contract, positive provider limits, and a web-search declaration. A new supplier model remains unavailable until the released upstream adapter and its replay, tool, image, and reasoning contracts are qualified.

## October catalog refresh
The Floret and Redeven refresh uses the same raw models.dev response, SHA-256 `a6af79756a8a8efb5fd3144a83bd01f333e503043998d5f26f3c98bf9181d36c`. [ChatGPT plan authentication](chatgpt-local-authentication.md) discovers the account-specific listed inventory and intersects these reviewed capabilities.

## Endpoint compatibility
Anthropic's SDK appends `v1/messages`.

Preserve existing configured bases; never save the literal template or silently move a key between regions. Native iOS settings link to official provider documentation for this choice.

## Published-engine adoption
Redeven currently consumes published Floret v7.78.2 with `GOWORK=off`; no sibling dependency or transport copy bypasses the upstream boundary.

New catalog entries receive an explicit search review; supplier search support does not imply an implemented or qualified Redeven search adapter.

The Runtime uses native Anthropic and Google list authentication/pagination and OpenAI-compatible inventories for supported brands. Unknown identities require explicit adapter-supported capability configuration. See [Model directory and selection](model-directory-and-selection.md) for ownership, deadlines, and scope isolation.

sections.body:
## Readiness and saving
The shared Flower composer follows the same credential contract as provider execution: a selected Ollama inventory model or configured OpenAI-compatible model can start or continue a conversation without a stored API key. Credential snapshots report actual secret presence; readiness must not manufacture a configured secret or bypass catalog membership.

Unknown discovered models require explicit capabilities before they become runnable.

## Field requirements
| Field | Required value or omission behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Provider API key | Optional for Ollama and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints; all other local-profile provider types require a new or stored key. Desktop and Redeven AI model sources retain their separate session authority. |
| Base URL | OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini may use their adapter default. Other provider types require an explicit HTTP(S) URL. |
| Provider display name | Optional; the UI derives a name from the provider type or identity. |
| Models | Explicit lists require named models; catalog providers save explicit `selected_models`, including an empty selection after deselecting all models. Unresolved legacy exclusion profiles require selection review; unavailable selected identities retain their metadata without requiring invented capacity. |
| Context and output limits | Published catalog or adapter defaults may supply omitted limits. Explicit compatible, OpenRouter, xAI, Groq, and Ollama model entries require context capacity. Custom catalog models also require it. Reviewed models retain their established optional output limits; unknown discovered models require explicit context, output, and tools capability. |
| Brave API key | Required only when Brave search is enabled; existing stored credentials satisfy the requirement. |

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Each local PTY uses Floret's execution and effect identities. `terminal.exec` waits 5 seconds by default (`yield_ms` omitted or zero), or a positive value capped at 30 seconds. When waiting ends, it returns a running process ID and the command continues.

`terminal.read` waits up to 10 seconds for output after the caller's sequence and returns early on output or exit. An empty timeout returns the running process ID with its cursor unchanged; the model decides whether to read again. `terminal.write` writes bounded stdin; `terminal.terminate` requests process-tree termination and waits for reap and output drain.

Browser payloads exclude local working paths, stdin, authorization proofs, and effect internals.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Redeven does not wait on authority barriers, admission receipts, recovery handles, or projection cursors. Terminal reads never trigger settlement retries. UI polling may refresh process bytes while a detail row is open, but it cannot synthesize canonical status or cause provider dispatch.

frontmatter.title: Tessiven Runtime discovery and operations

concepts.summary:
The Runtime-owned Tessiven product service is the authority for UI and Flower
Runtime discovery and dispatch. It composes the existing Desktop connection
registry, authenticated Gateway catalogs, Runtime business resource executors,
and Desktop lifecycle coordinator. Discovery observes registered paths without
starting a process or acquiring a business session. A reference identifies one
path; it grants no permission. Lost source authority, changed path generations,
replaced identities, and revoked permissions stop dispatch. A lost mutation
response reports an uncertain canonical tool outcome. The model first inspects
the original operation or current state before deciding what work remains; the
original invocation never replays automatically.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Official surface
- `tessiven.runtimes` / `GET /_redeven_proxy/api/tessiven/runtimes` returns   independent source availability and exact target paths. - `tessiven.runtime.inspect` / `POST .../runtimes/inspect` reads status,   bounded public diagnostics, or the original Desktop operation. - `tessiven.runtime.action` / `POST .../runtimes/actions` requests connection   or one supported `start`, `stop`, `restart`, or `update` process operation. - `tessiven.inspect/action` retain the canonical canvas version, bound instance,   and resource identity checks for Managed Services and containers.

No sibling module, replacement SDK, or product lifecycle queue is introduced.

## Source authority and discovery
Desktop registers its Tessiven host through owner-authenticated private Runtime control. Web Service, CodeSpace, nested frame, unrelated-origin and worker requests cannot declare a native source;

Ambiguous references fail closed.

## Connection and business access
Explicit connect reuses saved configuration and existing connection leases.

It cannot carry claimed permission flags, an arbitrary URL, another Runtime reference, or a process-lifecycle action.

Member removal and replacement retire the transport; no local or alternate route is substituted.

## Native lifecycle handoff
Process actions use saved direct Desktop placements and the existing [Desktop lifecycle owner](../desktop/desktop-runtime-process-lifecycle.md). The model cannot choose a download URL or release version; the existing release selector owns updates and post-operation verification.

Unknown connection outcomes require checking the selected connection in its native owner rather than retrying.

sections.body:

The Connected environments panel and Runtime node entry use this same service. The Runtime Dialog is part of the loaded Tessiven page; opening it must not suspend the page or show its navigation loading placeholder.

Gateway v6 application access, Tessiven DSL, and persistent database lineages retain their current shapes.

frontmatter.title: AI readiness and service generation lifecycle

concepts.summary:
- Authority: Floret owns durable Agent and Store facts; Redeven owns process-local AI availability and presentation.
- Outcome: non-AI product surfaces remain usable while AI startup inspects, migrates, verifies, recovers, or blocks.
- Invariants: one controller owns construction, retry, generation publication, request leases, drain, and close; each AI request stays on one generation.
- Failure boundary: unavailable or blocked startup returns a sanitized typed envelope, publishes no partial service, repairs no Store data, and never becomes durable Agent state.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Process-local readiness
The Code App composition layer owns the only AI readiness controller.

The startup order is unfinished replacement recovery, owner open and migration, canonical validation and persistent index reuse or first build, product preparation, explicit activation, then publication.

Retry is explicit, asynchronous, and admits at most one startup owner.

## Generation leases
Every ready service is published as one monotonically identified generation. The controller waits for every idempotent release, closes the old service once, and only then constructs and publishes a replacement.

Long-lived model-source calls receive the generation context so replacement can cancel their work before waiting for release.

## Route availability
AI lifecycle routes return HTTP 503 with machine code `AI_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and the current sanitized snapshot when no generation can be leased. Readiness, retry, stop, and administrator-only snapshot and restore routes never acquire a service.

Incomplete provider leases fail closed, release any supplied resource, and cannot be presented as `ready`.

## Maintenance presentation
See [Flower startup and recovery presentation](flower-startup-presentation.md) for Env App and Desktop admission, phase progress, stop/retry, focus and draft continuity.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
The readiness controller must not import Floret, SQLite, or threadstore packages; perform owner storage inspection; hold `runtime.Host` or `storage.Backend`; or retain canonical Agent DTOs.

Readiness history is not recovery authority.

concepts.summary:
Redeven owns container management as a native product capability. The
`containerengine` package is the only Docker and Podman execution layer shared
by native Containers and Web Services; `containerresource` is the only native
mutation, persistence, and reconciliation owner. Resources created by Web
Services remain visible but read-only in Containers. Unknown runtime targets, stale
preflights, ambiguous outcomes, and failed authoritative observation fail
closed without replaying mutations.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Runtime execution
[Container runtime execution](container-runtime-execution.md) owns active Docker/Podman discovery, endpoint binding, typed CLI reads and shared resource normalization. Native mutations and product permissions use that single execution owner.

## Native service boundary
Volume reference completeness and the independent disk usage read are owned by [Volume usage observation](container-volume-usage.md).

`containerresource` strictly decodes every mutation request and rejects unknown fields.

Unknown results remain explicit.

## Product ownership and permissions
The Local API is under `/_redeven_proxy/api/container-resources` and `/_redeven_proxy/api/container-resource-operations`. Server-side enforcement is authoritative; disabled UI controls are only a presentation aid.

Renderer cannot construct argv, skip validation, or use native mutation on managed resources.

## Data and host safety
DTOs expose only typed, redacted fields. They never return environment values, arbitrary label values, credentials, socket paths, certificates, remote URLs, or Compose file paths.

Ordinary terminal sessions retain their Write and Execute permission contract.

## Product surface
The native Activity and Workbench interaction, loading, resource-navigation, Compose input, and responsive presentation contracts are owned by [Native container console](container-resources-console.md). That surface may project only the targets and capabilities established here; it cannot create a second routing, mutation, or ownership path.

Resource readiness observes engine reachability directly; host-service state additionally identifies management capabilities and never substitutes for a successful resource probe.

frontmatter.title: Native container console

concepts.summary:
Containers is one native Activity and multi-instance Workbench surface over the
targets authorized by [Native container resources](container-resources-capability.md).
The console controller owns selection and navigation; the [resource snapshot contract](../ui/env-resource-cache.md) owns shared persisted presentation and refresh lifetime.
The UI never exposes endpoint selection, never commits a response from an old
target, and never creates a lifecycle path outside `containerresource`.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Stable console state
Each `redeven.containers` instance persists only its resource view and selected resource key. A resource always retains its source target; same-name Docker and Podman resources remain separate.

New resources use the sole compatible runtime directly or ask for Docker versus Podman inside the operation Dialog; actions on existing resources always reuse their source target.

## Resource presentation and navigation
One compact header owns refresh and Operations. It never exposes engine or endpoint selection, and Workbench hides a duplicate product title.

Operation progress and sanitized errors use the canonical [Native container operation observation](containers-operation-observation.md) surface.

## Compose input
A saved Compose Project contains one to eight ordered absolute YAML paths, one optional absolute env-file path, and up to sixteen profile names. The form owns these as arrays, never as newline- or comma-encoded backend strings.

The former directory-only data source and lazy picker compatibility wrapper do not remain as alternate paths.

## Container run input
Container creation has one `ContainerRunDraft` and one serializer.

Environment values and host paths are never persisted as UI state. The draft survives preflight and confirmation, is cleared only after a successful operation or explicit close, and reaches the existing preflight/hash/operation path rather than a second creation protocol.

## Responsive and accessible behavior
Desktop uses a compact sortable table, narrow Workbench hides secondary columns, and mobile uses cards with a full-screen detail page. Missing, stopped, unreachable, or permission-denied engines render a dedicated detection state rather than stale inventory.

## Visual feedback
Inventories, details, service configuration, creation forms, and operation observation share a restrained type hierarchy and semantic theme surfaces. Product hover and press feedback is brief; detail identity and disclosure entrances use small, bounded movements.

Dialog and menu positioning, focus, and lifecycle continue to belong to the released shared primitives.

frontmatter.title: Container service management

concepts.summary:
One `ContainerServiceController` owns Docker and Podman service discovery, lifecycle,
configuration, preflight identity, and reconciliation. Stable opaque service
IDs replace endpoints. Host mutations require full RWX and Admin, never elevate
privileges, and fail closed when ownership, revision, or final state is unknown.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Discovery and identity
The controller returns one independently detected service per engine. Detection never scans or falls back to another target.

The resource console uses the bounded engine-readiness contract in [Native container resources](container-resources-capability.md), so a slow host-management command cannot delay a stopped-daemon result.

## Lifecycle and authority
Lifecycle mutations are `container.services.start`, `container.services.stop`, and `container.services.restart`. Redeven never invokes `sudo`, `pkexec`, a password prompt, polkit, group membership changes, or socket permission changes.

The service stays locked until a fresh read proves final state; interrupted operations are never replayed.

## Configuration
`GET /_redeven_proxy/api/container-resources/services` requires Read and exposes only the configuration access mode and source IDs. One failed source never hides another source.

Its contiguous migrations map legacy service state to `engine` and rename the retired `client_proxy` source to `docker_cli`.

## Product surface and observation
The Containers header exposes one direct Settings action for “Container services”; runtime warnings decorate that same action instead of adding a second entry. Refresh preserves the last authoritative cards, animates only the refresh indicator, and reports failure inline; it never replaces usable content with a skeleton or replays card-entry animation.

Refresh and operation completion reload authoritative service, runtime, inventory, and Web Service state.

sections.body: - `containerengine` owns service discovery, exact host argv, candidate   validation, atomic replacement, rollback, and authoritative observation. - `containerresource` owns permission-independent preflight data, Admin impact,   operation locks, durable sanitized state, and reconciliation. - The Code App Local API owns authenticated Read/RWX/Admin enforcement and   no-store configuration delivery. - Docker Desktop retains ownership of private application settings; Podman   Machine and remote host tools retain ownership of non-local configuration. - The host administrator owns installation and operating-system authority.

concepts.summary:
Redeven's container engine owns volume observations; the native resource service
binds them to the authorized active runtime. Container references include stopped
containers, and disk usage reports occupied space rather than capacity. Partial
inspection cannot establish that a volume is unused. A failed or unsupported
size read leaves the inventory usable and the size unavailable. Neither
observation replaces the current authoritative mutation preflight.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Reference completeness
Volume inventory and detail return `referenced_containers`, `used_by`, and `references_complete`. The native console renders incomplete observations as Unknown and excludes them from both In use and Unused filters. A partial Used by view may show known references together with an incomplete-inspection notice.

## Disk usage
`GET /container-resources/volume-disk-usage` is an independent, Read-only, no-store observation. Unexpected layouts fail visibly instead of being interpreted as an empty measurement.

Disk usage never authorizes cleanup or overrides the reference preflight.

concepts.title: Native container operation observation
concepts.description: Keep endpoint-bound native mutations locked until authoritative reconciliation proves a terminal outcome.

frontmatter.description: Keep endpoint-bound native mutations locked until authoritative reconciliation proves a terminal outcome.
frontmatter.title: Native container operation observation

concepts.summary:
Every native Containers mutation has one durable Redeven operation identity and
one resource-local lock. Submission, cancellation, progress events, restart
recovery, and terminal reconciliation flow through `containerresource`.
Inventory refreshes and UI observation never become a second lifecycle owner.
Lost submissions, stale plans, runtime restarts, and unavailable engines are
reported explicitly and are never hidden behind automatic replay.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Admission and serialization
The operation key contains engine, opaque endpoint ID, resource kind, and canonical identity.

Reusing a request ID with different hashes produces an idempotency conflict instead of a second operation.

## Execution, cancellation, and events
The service owns an operation context from queued state through reconciliation. Cancellation is an explicit API action; closing Activity, Workbench, an inspector, an event stream, or the browser never implies cancellation.

Terminal errors use a small public taxonomy for storage, registry availability, rate limiting, not-found, and access denial; the drawer presents that sanitized code and message with the durable timeline.

## Authoritative terminal observation
After engine execution returns, the service reloads the exact endpoint-bound resource or relevant bounded inventory.

The operation is never replayed, regardless of whether the resource appears present or absent.

## UI observation
Inventory requests and streams are fenced by source runtime, endpoint, resource view, and request generation. A superseded response cannot replace current data.

Mobile and desktop expose the same state and cancellation authority.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: - The database is operation evidence, not a mutation queue or replay journal. - UI inventory and SSE consumers observe service authority; they do not own   lifecycle state or reconciliation. - A runtime restart converts active work to interrupted after read-only   observation; it never assumes success or retries the command. - The full native container ownership contract is defined in   [Native container resources](container-resources-capability.md).

frontmatter.title: Database schema migration ownership

concepts.summary:
- Authority: each repository migrates the schemas it owns; Redeven owns product databases, while Floret and ReDevPlugin own their internal stores.
- Outcome: each Redeven product store opens through an exact versioned schema contract before the dependent service accepts requests.
- Invariants: released migration lineages are contiguous, atomic, verified, and data-preserving; existing-file preflight reads the complete SQLite main-plus-WAL view, while future, drifted, wrong-kind, and unsupported inputs fail without changing database files or sidecars.
- Failure boundary: a failed migration stops the affected service with the previous supported database intact; Redeven never patches an upstream database or silently replaces an incompatible product database.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Redeven-owned stores
Each SQLite store declares a stable database kind, current version, supported minimum version, ordered `n -> n+1` migrations, an existing-schema validator, and a final exact verifier.

Migration and verification failure rolls back.

Host identity upgrades use their own private journal and native verification after Registry migration; no live-engine guess or database reset substitutes for resource ownership.

## Upstream-owned stores
Floret owns canonical thread storage and its schema lifecycle through the published Runtime APIs.

Cross-database atomicity is never assumed or simulated by copying upstream lifecycle state into Redeven tables.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Automatic migration is not permission to accept arbitrary historical shapes. A repository-owned pre-release reset is exceptional, user-approved, and permanently closes once its new baseline is distributed.

frontmatter.title: Env App session event transport

concepts.summary: Floe Webapp owns one HTTP proxy runtime per connected Env App session. All built-in browser event subscriptions and the ReDevPlugin host request adapter use that runtime's logical streams. They cannot occupy native HTTP/1.1 connection slots, choose another upstream or identity, or create a second transport. Session replacement and teardown cancel old observations. Each feature retains its existing recovery policy; stopping observation never cancels background business work.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## One session and one request path
Product subscriptions call the Shell-bound session event reader. Floe Webapp's acquisition lifecycle opens a logical HTTP stream on the current Flowersec session and parses SSE with its shared bounded parser.

Session multiplexing removes those event requests from the browser HTTP pool; changing request priority alone cannot do so.

## Authority and resource lifetime
Local session issuance declares only Env App API and plugin API paths plus the plugin CSRF and expected-management-revision headers. Remote issuers must declare the same plugin request authority and upload cap in their signed scope.

Product code must not reset a successful response while its bytes are still being consumed.

## Observation and recovery
Flower maintains one workspace stream; thread selection never reconnects it.

Its transport and cancellation regression coverage remain intact.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: An observer cannot choose another upstream, session identity or native HTTP transport. Ending an observation does not cancel the feature's background business operation.

frontmatter.title: Git workspace inventory lifecycle

concepts.summary: Redeven exposes Git workspace state as bounded, immutable, process-local inventory snapshots. Fresh queries stream Git porcelain output into an admitted snapshot; paged and path-scoped reads bind an exact revision. Git and Files mutations coordinate against the same repository and topology authority, invalidate all affected snapshots before and after effects, and never use display state to authorize a mutation. Oversized, stale, malformed, or resource-exhausted work fails closed with a small typed Git error while the Flowersec session remains usable.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Inventory
Workspace capture reads NUL-delimited porcelain v2 incrementally. Token, record, canonical-path, retained-heap, subprocess, capture, and published-cache limits are admitted before retained capacity grows beyond its reservation.

Stable filesystem identity prevents a deleted and recreated path from inheriting an older coordinator or revision.

## Query and wire
`git.getCapabilities` advertises revisioned workspace pages, path-scoped status, directory scope, and stash-section diff support. `git.listWorkspacePathStatuses` accepts only a bounded set of already-known paths and returns file rows or aggregate directory counts without descendant arrays.

It does not claim a general bound for non-Git outbound responses or notifications; transport-wide lifecycle remains owned by the published Flowersec v5.10.3 release.

## Mutation coordination
The Agent owns one Git runtime shared by direct sessions. A cancellable topology gate, active-worktree registry, canonical repository lock order, per-repository fair read/write coordination, epochs, process admissions, snapshot storage, and destructive-scan admission form one lifecycle.

Descendants that deliberately escape the process group remain an explicit operating-system boundary; their existence does not permit an unbounded handler or retained pipe.

## Linked worktree removal
Linked-worktree lists and previews expose summary state rather than full file arrays. The root Git control entry is excluded only after its type, exact contents when applicable, canonical target, and filesystem identity match the already resolved Git directory.

Hostile external writers and metadata outside the portable fingerprint, including ACLs, extended attributes, resource forks, and alternate data streams, are explicit non-transactional boundaries.

sections.body: Git remains authoritative for repository and workspace state; snapshots are process-local read models and never authorize mutations. Floret, ReDevPlugin, Flowersec transport internals, non-Git outbound RPC allocation, and operating-system processes that deliberately escape the supervised process group remain outside this runtime's ownership.

concepts.summary:

backpressure for remote desktop and host application windows. Redeven owns the
resource, user authorization and route mapping. All graphical data, including
state, attachment tickets, input, clipboard, audio, pixels and explicit disconnect,

remain on the authenticated browser entry. Missing authority fails closed; no

sections.body:

Window creation must not reintroduce a raw HTTP step between session admission and the resource-scoped viewer connection. Missing session transport fails closed.

## One session boundary for every backend
The viewer's `WindowTransport` maps product paths into the published `flowersec-proxy/http1` and `flowersec-proxy/ws` stream APIs.

The product's native application attachment keeps a bounded event queue.

Generic Code App injection must not install a second transport on these marked graphical documents.

sections.title: Boundaries

## Resource authority
Acquisition requires read, write and execute permissions and an active resource owned by the authenticated user. Its exact spend target identifies the window kind, environment, port-forward application and forward ID; launcher, Runtime and application origins must all match.

A view-only session keeps the full access requirement.

## Recovery and browser capability
Carrier failure clears the cached proxy runtime.

HTTPS or a trustworthy local origin is still required where the browser restricts those APIs; product code does not mark an insecure network origin as trustworthy.

frontmatter.title: Cross-platform host application behavior

concepts.summary:
Host Applications separates viewing, sharing, window closure and process exit on
both platforms. Ordinary actions preserve unsaved work and respect app cancellation.
Only an independently confirmed Force quit may bypass saving. The backend owns
process evidence, and the interface names the actual supported operation. OS
session, display and service policies remain authoritative; unavailable recovery
must not silently relaunch an unrelated or replacement process.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
| Operation | macOS | Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Close outer Desktop window / browser popup | Release this client lease; app survives | Same |
| Network loss, reload, second viewer | Reconnect same live app; stale input is revoked | Same |
| Release this client lease | End this capture/route; other clients and app survive | End this proxy/route; other clients and app survive |
| No window for more than 40 seconds | Waiting, with native menu/reopen | Waiting, reconnect same process without relaunch |
| Close last window | Viewer closes; app decides whether its process exits | Same |
| Cancel normal close/quit | Preserve application and save dialog | Same; ordinary control is Close all windows |
| Explicit Force quit in library | Confirm loss warning; exact AppKit instance | Confirm loss warning; exact owned backend and descendants |
| Orderly Runtime shutdown or process exit | Native app remains discoverable | Private display survives; new Runtime verifies/reconnects it |
| Running list | Regular apps in the logged-in OS session | Caller-owned Redeven instances, including detached/windowless apps |
| Host reboot / display server destruction / OS cleanup | No survival guarantee | Same; Runtime cgroup cleanup may also end its virtual display |

## Accepted operations and visible state
Quit and force-quit requests are asynchronous. The Host Applications surface must close the confirmation dialog after acceptance and show a per-application pending state until the authoritative running snapshot confirms the target instance is gone.

The first Force quit action only enters that state; only its final confirmation sends the destructive host request.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Linux cannot generically request AppKit-style application quit or reopen, nor adopt an arbitrary process on another display. macOS requires its real logged-in graphical session and explicit capture/input permissions. Neither backend can preserve an application after its OS or display environment has been destroyed.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Client ownership
Redeven embeds `@floegence/floe-webapp-core/remote-input` and its stylesheet from the published package.

Copy, cut and paste have one handler per backend and cannot also produce an IME submission.

Platform adapters flush pending pointer output before sending keys, text or clipboard actions to preserve input order.

## Linux native delivery
The combined backend consumes the published helper protocol through an authenticated Runtime stream. It never registers another composition or gesture owner.

System clipboard normalization belongs to the browser/OS; confirmed Unicode remains byte-exact.

## Retained Xpra delivery
Released `floe-native-apps` owns the capability probe, private input environment, commit-only xcb-imdkit XIM bridge, GTK3/GTK4/Qt5/Qt6 context adapters, prepared HTML client and authenticated Xpra input scheduler.

Linux never rejects the whole viewer because an application's historical preparation version differs.

No loaded module is replaced and no process is killed.

## macOS delivery
Native window snapshots advertise `input_version: 1`. Production code never switches the host's global input source.

Same-window recapture can retain local focus but rejects input until the replacement frame is decoded.

## Verification boundary
The [validation record](../operations/host-application-input-validation.md) distinguishes controller event simulation, real app text receipts, real OS IME input and actual mobile-device evidence. A sent packet, mobile viewport emulation or synthetic composition event alone does not establish system input-method acceptance.

The [preparation owner](host-application-preparation.md) selects complete components.

Support claims require real package and desktop evidence, as recorded in the [validation owner](../operations/host-application-platform-validation.md).

The [native macOS contract](macos-host-applications.md) owns local launch, remote single-window capture, input, and graceful lifecycle. macOS 13 or newer uses the packaged `redeven-computer-host` helper.

A Mac without a graphical login cannot create a private headless AppKit session. Native AppKit applications do not become X11 applications by installing XQuartz, and Xpra desktop shadowing is not this implementation.

A touch begins pending, without a remote button press.

Both motion paths use the same target authority, microtask coalescing, explicit flush and cancellation; platform bindings must not install another raw-event listener.

Leaving the document does cancel.

## Scroll and lifecycle
A finger moving up or left reveals content below or to the right.

The Linux native adapter submits fractional CSS-pixel deltas directly; its gesture release callback has no remainder and never releases keyboard input.

Each viewer owns its controller, feedback and transient remainder independently.

## Acceptance boundary
[Validation](../operations/host-application-validation.md) distinguishes generated browser events from actual native application receipts and physical mobile devices. Device emulation cannot qualify a real soft keyboard or pinch.

routes, private state placement, localized preparation and the user's pending app
opening. Applications execute on the host. Preparation never requires a container,

## Component ownership and admission
Redeven consumes `github.com/floegence/floe-native-apps` v0.22.19 as a published Go module, built with the same Go 1.27.2 toolchain.

Partial managed and system installations are never merged into a synthetic toolset.

The [host application contract](host-applications.md) owns restoration of the application's environment, private display isolation and host-owned dependencies.

## Preparation execution and recovery
Reading status, explicitly inspecting a transfer plan and observing events requires read permission. The upstream serializes writers with its private-root lease and enforces owner-scoped cancellation and idempotent request/chunk admission.

The [Desktop component cache contract](../desktop/host-application-component-cache.md) owns cross-device reuse, seven-day idle retention, the 2 GB archive budget, process leases and separate cache/download/transfer presentation.

## Window and permission interaction
Selecting an unavailable application presents preparation for that actual app. An in-flight session-only refresh must not reuse the old unavailable state or prevent the pending window from opening once.

Its bundled helper, native local opening and explicit remote screen-recording/accessibility authorization follow the [macOS contract](macos-host-applications.md); a graphical login is still required.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Graphical state and every backend's picture/input connection use the [Flowersec window transport](graphical-window-transport.md). The viewer owns the presentation and recovery rules below.

## Browser launch admission
The catalog reserves a browser tab in the initiating click and keeps application identity visible while launch and route admission run. Retry uses the host's existing launch deduplication; closing the tab while admission is pending never cancels or kills a session that the host may have admitted.

Browser loading documents explicitly omit Desktop chrome and must not depend on Node globals.

## Connection and terminal presentation
The localized bootstrap owns connection presentation. A launcher that exits before opening any window produces an actionable launch failure instead of an endless waiting page; this must not impose a timeout on a live, slow-starting process.

Terminal records are bounded in memory and do not survive Runtime restart; an expired document route may no longer be served, and users must reopen from the library rather than rely on an old viewer URL.

## Rendering ownership
The [display contract](host-application-display.md) owns SDK layouts, density, cursor coordinates and native window-state mapping. First-pixel and terminal state decisions remain here; neither resource nor geometry notifications prove application exit.

New combined Linux sessions use the Runtime canvas viewer and the released native frame/input/cursor protocol.

Its pre-client script inherits the owning viewer's Flowersec constructor, and missing transport fails closed.

The snapshot becomes ineligible for resource lookup; other active shares and the application remain independent.

## Capability and recovery boundary
One SDK result determines which operations are available:

| Result | Redeven behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Current viewer, compatible backend/input | Connect to the surviving app and preserve content |
| Missing, corrupt or unsupported current viewer resources | Report preparation failure and offer retry |
| Display protocol older than 2 | Use logical density; explain the high-resolution limitation |
| Unsupported input or ordered pointer protocol | Disable affected input; retain pictures and local controls |
| Authenticated incompatible process-module registration | Explain saving and normal application exit before reopening |
| Missing input context, temporary focus loss or ordinary disconnect | Preserve existing recovery semantics without inferring a version problem |

Document and asset content therefore cannot diverge through the application's old HTTP resource tree.

concepts.summary:
- Authority: the application owns its business execution; Redeven owns authorized lifecycle actions, native process identity, launch records, and opening validation.
- Outcome: Desktop or Runtime exit, restart, or upgrade leaves a launched service's PID and launch generation unchanged.
- Invariants: no new binary, resident supervisor, application-specific driver branch, process-output pipe to Runtime, or ownership inferred from PID alone.
- Recovery boundary: absent, mismatched, and uninspectable resources are distinct. Only confirmed absence permits eligible automatic startup; opening failure never stops a running application.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Independent execution
Host launches in its own session and process group. The foreground start contract remains: templates must not double-fork, background the application, or retain a permanent wrapper.

This is not a resident service supervisor or another binary.

## Native identity and recovery
The `host:v3` identity binds service ID, launch nonce, PID, and a digest of native facts:

New identities never use formatted dates, timezone, command text, or `kern.boottime`.

An old process's inherited output descriptors cannot be replaced externally; independent output handling takes effect on its next explicit restart.

## Opening and presentation
Host supplies verified native launch identity and executes only the applied authorized hooks through the common [managed opening contract](managed-web-service-opening.md). The driver stores only launch facts and after-start hook completion, never executable snapshots or a second entrance cache. Preparation follows healthy startup and can be retried without stopping the application.

Imported Host templates receive `REDEVEN_TEMPLATE_DIR` pointing to the active original source directory for helper files; [Git source review](managed-service-git-sources.md) prevents replacement during associated service operations and opening hooks.

concepts.title: Linux application instances and independent sharing
concepts.description: Preserve owned Linux graphical applications across viewer and Runtime lifetimes, with verified recovery and explicit process termination.

frontmatter.description: Preserve owned Linux graphical applications across viewer and Runtime lifetimes, with verified recovery and explicit process termination.
frontmatter.title: Linux application instances and independent sharing

concepts.summary:
Redeven owns Linux application instances, caller authorization and ephemeral
sharing; the published Floe Native Apps module owns GIO launch and process-tree
observation. A live application outlives its viewers and window count. Closing a
viewer, releasing a share lease or exiting Runtime never requests application termination.
After Runtime restart, the same host user and private state can recover a surviving
backend only after matching its kernel process generation and private endpoint
identity. No persisted PID alone authorizes signaling. Destroying the virtual
display, a host reboot or external cgroup cleanup cannot preserve an application dependent on that display.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Instance and sharing ownership
One instance has an opaque ID, authorized owner, application metadata, kernel boot/PID/start identity, component identity, backend and versioned private record. The endpoint binds the same instance and private socket; a reusable window ID or persisted PID alone never grants authority.

Redeven never changes that policy.

## Launch and readiness
The published supervisor owns GIO launch, descendant/sandbox identity, launcher exit status and application lifetime. Preparation, actual launcher failure, application exit, window presence and first pixels are separate observations.

Xpra retains its published readiness, final-window and audio-disable contracts.

## Browser profile ownership
Redeven supplies one stable private browser-profile directory per authorized owner and catalog application under its canonical state root.

An observed process-tree exit before its first window is an explicit no-window launch failure even when the exit status is zero; a still-live process can continue waiting.

## Normal close and explicit force quit
The Linux ordinary operation is named Close all windows because these Linux backends have no universal application-level graceful quit API.

This path never follows ordinary close, disconnect, save cancellation or an uncertain response automatically. An accepted request is not proof of process exit; running snapshots remove the row only when the kernel confirms termination.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Recovery requires the original private state and host OS user. A host reboot, external process cleanup or destroyed compositor/X server cannot be repaired by reconnecting. Ordinary closure always preserves native save/cancel decisions.

frontmatter.title: Local UI surface

concepts.summary: Redeven Local UI is the Runtime-owned client endpoint. Desktop and browsers can connect concurrently using independent access sessions. Public HTTP/WS or HTTPS/WSS shares one configured port; authenticated Desktop bridge traffic remains on its separate numeric-loopback listener and isolated `flowersec-private-loopback/1` profile. The versioned SQLite authority store is the sole issuer-side source for one-shot Flowersec authorization and browser spend state across all transports. [Local UI network exposure](../security/local-ui-network-exposure.md) owns protocol choice, scope, password, certificate, and migration rules.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
`localui.Server` is built with an agent, Code App app server, bind spec, runtime-control socket path, Local Environment identity, diagnostics store, and optional access gate.

Local UI bind parsing accepts `localhost`, canonical loopback IP literals, concrete non-loopback unicast IPv4 and IPv6 literals, and the `0.0.0.0` and `::` wildcards.

In-process maps retain only active-session cleanup projections and never authorize a request.

## Concurrent shutdown
Context cancellation and explicit shutdown enter the same serialized close path. Runtime-control and management status serialize start/close and protect endpoint reads, so overlapping shutdown cannot dereference cleared servers or advertise a retired control listener. This uses bounded in-process locks and does not introduce durable lifecycle state.

## Session event observation
All built-in Env App event subscriptions use the current authenticated Flowersec session's HTTP proxy. Short bootstrap requests and native file/media requests stay independent of session acquisition.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Process and channel ownership
The Runtime must not start a separate persistent capture helper for each application.

Empty channel inventory leaves the helper idle until the Runtime closes, so the next application uses the same ScreenCaptureKit process identity.

## Physical desktop integration
The exact released `FloeNativeDesktop` package owns reusable capture and native desktop input. Desktop media uses a separate binary pipe and bounded per-channel queues so pictures do not serialize behind control messages.

## Failure and shutdown
Each response channel has a bounded 128-message queue, preserving the supported operation-result burst.

Native applications and their unsaved work survive this shutdown.

**Running applications** uses AppKit's current regular application processes, including direct native launches, windowless applications and apps opened outside Redeven.

The request contains the selected bundle identity and opaque instance identifiers derived from canonical bundle path, PID and launch time.

A failed viewer opening also never rolls back a host session based on stale catalog state.

concepts.summary:
The macOS helper owns the menu exposed by a single-application viewer. It omits
the entire system Apple subtree and identified cross-application visibility
commands before issuing handles. Application titles remain literal native text.
Only an enabled leaf from the current snapshot, still under its allowed live
ancestry, can execute. Rejected or stale actions produce the existing localized
operation error and preserve the application and capture. Menu inspection happens
on explicit menu requests and actions, never on the launch or first-frame path.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Native menu projection
Read the bound application's main AX menu bar. macOS reserves its leading entry for the system Apple menu; omit that subtree structurally, independently of its title, host language or application name.

Empty, fully filtered or truncated submenus must never turn into executable leaf actions.

The application name is the first exposed menu group; there is no separate system-menu replacement or permanent warning.

## Handle lifetime and execution
Menu handles bind to the current application and capture/wait generation.

Removed, relocated, newly excluded, disabled or non-leaf items fail without being pressed.

The [native session contract](macos-host-applications.md) owns capture, input and window generations; this policy does not expand capture to other processes.

sections.body: Accessibility does not describe every command's effects. Direct local native launch keeps the host's normal macOS menu bar unchanged.

frontmatter.title: macOS application picture quality and delivery

concepts.summary:
Redeven's native application capture helper owns image resolution and encoding;
the viewer owns picture preferences and measured display statistics. Application
identity, permissions and input retain the [native session contract](macos-host-applications.md).
A frame can acknowledge delivery only after decoding for the current capture
generation. Quality changes and reconnects preserve the application process.
Hardware or browser video unavailability selects the explicit image transport;
the quality panel reports the transport actually producing frames. A real capture
failure retains the session's existing reconnect boundary.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Resolution and picture controls
Capture dimensions use the smaller of the viewer's device-pixel ratio, the native window's pixel density, and the chosen longest-edge limit.

Opening settings never resizes the app.

Limits are bounded and validated by the native helper.

## Encoders and delivery
A browser advertising H.264 WebCodecs software decoding can receive VideoToolbox hardware video. Hardware encoder unavailability uses JPEG images; a browser decoder failure explicitly renegotiates image transport.

Unchanged resize requests retain frame credit.

## Observable statistics and limits
Runtime diagnostics record connection-to-first-frame duration and generation; the browser debug log measures connection-to-first-decoded-frame duration.

High latency, host capture, encoding, browser decoding and network capacity can reduce achieved frame rate; a 60 FPS limit is not a guarantee of 60 FPS delivery.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Decoded frames acknowledge only the current capture generation. Picture preferences cannot change process or permission ownership. Video unavailability uses the declared image transport, while a capture failure retains the existing session recovery boundary.

concepts.summary:
Redeven's native helper owns macOS application-window lifetime. Its registry binds
exact AX windows to the selected process instance; capture surfaces do not define
window lifetime. Only confirmed destruction can start the last-window grace.
Uncertain inventory, unavailable capture and transport loss retain the session and
its recovery entrypoint while revoking stale input. Runtime preserves the helper's
explicit end reason; the shared viewer owns whether an established page can close.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Waiting and process lifetime
A running process without its first shareable window remains attached indefinitely; there is no first-window termination deadline. Releasing the current client lease during this wait ends that sharing lease normally; missing pixels do not turn a lease release into a launch failure. An unexpected helper exit is a failed sharing session, not evidence that the host application ended.

## Window evidence
The window registry distinguishes present, unknown and confirmed-empty inventories. No first-window deadline is introduced.

## Capture and recovery
Capture availability is independent of lifetime. AX identity survives a capture-surface replacement while the input generation is renewed; retired callbacks cannot update the replacement. Failure to launch and unexpected helper loss remain failures; missing pixels do not change a confirmed process exit into a failed launch.

## Terminal state
Terminal state retains the native end reason: `application_exited` confirms the bound process exited, `windows_closed` confirms its last shared window closed, and `sharing_stopped` confirms detachment. Closing windows and stopping sharing never claim the process has quit. The [lifecycle validation matrix](../operations/host-application-lifecycle.md) separates automated recovery evidence from OS/application compatibility limits.

frontmatter.title: Native macOS host applications

concepts.summary:
Redeven's macOS adapter owns native host application discovery and human-operated
window sessions. Application identity comes from installed bundles. A trusted
Desktop local-environment route launches the real app directly; remote access
captures the selected application's actual window, including an already running
single-instance app. Apps run as the Runtime user,
without containers, virtual machines, X11 or an independent desktop. The existing
[host application authorization](host-applications.md) applies to every operation
and stream. Missing permissions or graphical login block streaming explicitly.
Network loss preserves the app; reconnection attaches to the same process. Explicit
quit is independent of sharing and binds to the selected OS process generations.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Catalog and local launch
AppKit discovers applications in standard system/user application directories, running application bundle paths, and explicit custom absolute `.app` paths. Canonical bundle paths define identity; localized bundle metadata and system icons define presentation.

The [application management contract](macos-application-management.md) owns live OS inventory, explicit quit confirmation, process-generation validation and the distinction between quitting an app and stopping its sharing session.

## Remote window ownership and transport
The [native capture owner](macos-application-capture-owner.md) uses one Swift process and host-application protocol 2, separate from Computer Use. The helper verifies the returned canonical bundle path and binds its process, so single-instance applications reuse their existing windows.

Local focus during same-window recapture grants no remote input authority; composition begun before decoded pixels cannot acquire permission by waiting for a frame.

## Human control and lifecycle
Remote input shares the host's real graphical session and foreground. Explicit input activates and raises the bound window; foreground identity, focused AX window and pointer hit ownership must be verified before injection.

Protected content, inaccessible custom controls, separate-process dialogs, and apps with unusual window ownership require application-specific validation. macOS 13 API compatibility is a build contract, not a claim of testing every OS version, Intel host or third-party application.

sections.body: Every operation and stream keeps Host Applications authorization. Network loss preserves the application; reconnect binds the same process, and quitting remains independent of viewer closure.

concepts.summary:

- Outcome: public/private GitHub templates import through Desktop transfer or direct Runtime download without an installed `git` executable.
- Invariants: no background source checks, automatic source updates, dependency installation, script execution, application upgrade, or restart occurs during source import/review. Credentials remain request-scoped.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Acquisition and credentials
The template center exposes Import from GitHub and Check template updates.

It never fetches application packages, npm dependencies, or images.

UI transfer requests have a 24 MiB encoded-body ceiling.

## Review and confirmation
The import dialog separates source entry, directory selection, and final review.

The import flow uses a fixed-height frame bounded by the viewport and its Workbench surface.

The source digest participates in install/update review and applied Runtime identity, so a helper-only edit cannot reuse an obsolete reviewed operation.

## Atomic directory ownership
`<managed-state>/template-sources/source_<opaque-id>/` contains the original files only.

An uncertain commit never deletes a potentially active directory; retry receipts and startup cleanup resolve complete unclaimed directories. Startup removes only unreferenced source directories, never repairs or replaces a corrupt active source.

sections.body: Host hooks receive `REDEVEN_TEMPLATE_DIR` for original helper files. [Registry migration](database-schema-migrations.md) owns the contiguous version-4-to-5 metadata migration and atomic rollback.
