sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Reproducible measurements
Compare baseline and candidate on the same host, browser version, source size and workload.

An SSH tunnel changes transport overhead and must be recorded.

| Metric | Definition and controlled viewer acceptance budget |
| --- | --- |
| Input to presented pixels | DOM key event through remote application to changed canvas pixels on the next animation frame; nearest-rank P95 of 20 samples below 150 ms in every mode |
| Input during motion | The same 20-sample measurement while document scroll continues; P95 below 250 ms, including Save data cadence |
| Presented FPS | At most one changed-canvas presentation per animation frame; Motion first at least 25 FPS during document scroll |
| Received payload | All incoming WebSocket data bytes, including JSON; excludes WebSocket/TLS/SSH framing and network retransmissions |
| Idle bandwidth | Below 0.25 Mb/s after settling; a fully unchanged document should send zero image bytes |
| Document-motion bandwidth | Below 5 Mb/s for Automatic/Clarity/Save data and 15 Mb/s for Motion first at the recorded source size |
| Decode work | No more than two current-target frames plus one retired decode; no reconnect on a picture change |
| First frame | Navigation to first decoded canvas presentation; excludes browser-process launch before the viewer attaches |

## Published-module product results
A sandboxed Chrome 153 client on Ubuntu passed all v0.21.0 viewer budgets over loopback, isolating capture, forwarding, decoding and presentation from networking:

| Application | Automatic Mb/s | Motion-first FPS | Static-input P95 across modes | Scrolling-input P95 across modes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chrome | 2.14 | 27.0 | 46–65 ms | 129–237 ms |
| Firefox | 4.37 | 37.4 | 65–81 ms | 99–231 ms |

## Observed native pipeline improvement
Sequential tests on Ubuntu 26.04 amd64, Chrome 153.0.8010.36 (1292 by 753 pixels) and Firefox 155.0.1 (1000 by 700 pixels) compared the authentic v0.20.0 component with the v0.21.0 implementation.

| Workload | v0.20.0 | Automatic | Motion first | Save data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chrome scroll, Mb/s | 25.04 | 1.59 | 10.61 | 0.64 |
| Chrome scroll, FPS | 25.1 | 19.4 | 34.0 | 8.8 |
| Chrome input P95, ms | 59.6 | 52.8 | 49.9 | 81.3 |
| Firefox scroll, Mb/s | 30.64 | 2.20 | 6.53 | 0.59 |
| Firefox scroll, FPS | 32.4 | 28.7 | 37.4 | 7.9 |
| Firefox input P95, ms | 103.3 | 54.5 | 54.5 | 78.3 |

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Implementation And Distribution
Upstream commit `ec0d9cc8e64fd3e9e2020da017bec57a56ce0f94` replaces full-frame Python allocation and copying with a bounded Gst buffer pool.

These results certify the tested host-desktop component, not the whole optional application distribution.

## Correctness
Thirty-six focused Python tests pass, including existing damage, sequence, mapping and cursor rules.

- BGRA, BGRx, RGBA and RGBx; packed, padded and non-aligned source rows. - Separate cursor updates and embedded composition without corrupting retained clean pixels. - Bounded pool capacity, final-frame recovery, parent lease retention and interruptible shutdown. - Retained frame bytes after pool deactivation and idempotent capture close.

These checks retain the cursor, mode, reconnect and permission contracts; neither a debug workspace nor sibling source overlay is used.

## Performance Of The Final Implementation
The same udesk24 VM ran alternating old/new/old/new tests at 2560 by 1440 with software x264. The real private PipeWire producer emits a moving rectangle through MemFd at 60 FPS and never reads the user desktop.

| New B1 | 59.90 | 2.79 ms | 11.65 / 13.01 ms |
| Old A2 | 46.86 | 19.96 ms | 29.94 / 52.37 ms |
| New B2 | 59.90 | 2.64 ms | 8.68 / 9.99 ms |

| Run | Paint confirmations per second | Capture entry to returned paint ACK, median / P95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Old A1 | 32.78 | 68.89 / 140.23 ms |
| New B1 | 60.07 | 24.19 / 25.36 ms |
| Old A2 | 26.19 | 99.17 / 144.48 ms |
| New B2 | 60.01 | 14.89 / 17.29 ms |

## Deployment And Host Identity

| Interaction | Observed host or Viewer outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Picture | Physical GNOME panel and Clash Verge, then the fullscreen task GTK fixture, appear in the real Viewer. |
| Mouse | A real Viewer click increments the fixture's visible button counter and host event log. |
| Keyboard | Physical `a` press/release reaches GTK; twenty later presses add exactly twenty `a` characters to the host document. |

| Shortcut | The first Alt+Tab submission lacked host-effect evidence. A later real shortcut switches from the GTK fixture to Clash Verge and back. Only the latter observations qualify window switching. |
| Fullscreen | The real Viewer enters Electron fullscreen; Escape restores native window controls while retaining the remote picture. |
| Explicit disconnect | Picture is removed, input and shortcut controls are disabled, and **Desktop disconnected** instructs the user to close and reconnect. Closing and reopening from Env App previously restored the picture. |

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Published Dependency And Conditions
Both product binaries use clean source `6caee6df1da1eabdd5d9f4670d6eedcb578de1a3` and published `floe-native-apps` v0.22.6 (`dec4e3f48dba9445704b08cf2ff78c683c0c679a`).

Its glibc CUDA library cannot load into the isolated musl stack, which selects x264.

This is alternative scanout, not native 1440p60.

## Current Product Results
### macOS v0.22.6

| Capture | Minimum FPS | Maximum interval P95 | Maximum refinement | Bandwidth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1920x1080 | 57.582 | 23ms | 329.5ms | 14.71-14.82Mbps |
| 2560x1440 | 57.657 | 24.7ms | 351.1ms | 26.21-26.33Mbps |

Doubling acquisition from about 115 to 224 reads/s improved changed/encoded FPS only from 56.0 to 56.5; that higher-cost change was not adopted.

It had at most one pending handoff and zero at completion.

## Release And Lifecycle Evidence
v0.22.6 source CI, CodeQL, both native architectures, private applications, host-desktop media and Swift checks passed.

Authenticated Xvfb checks passed pixels, resource lifetime, protocol isolation, cursor, input and recovery. macOS uses a bounded latest-sample mailbox to separate comparison from encoding; callback wait P95 fell from about 8.6ms to 0.02ms.

Final focused desktop/appserver race tests were repeated against the published dependency and passed.

The implementation and subsequent records were fast-forwarded into local `main` through `2945183a90e46f382410fa7ae23d4b35d8b63998`, preserving existing unpublished commits.

Its performance is outside this delivery's acceptance scope by explicit user instruction; no 55 FPS Wayland claim is made. - Any broader release claim requires its own host qualification; source integration alone is not release acceptance.

At both 1920x1080 and 2560x1440, measure scrolling and task-owned window motion for at least 60 seconds, three times each, on a documented low-latency connection.

Refinement must finish within 500ms and match a lossless text reference at the same dimensions after host motion stops. 4K does not substitute for either required resolution.

## Reproduction And Repair
The ordinary Desktop connection to `udesk24`, using its normal saved portal grant, progressed from authorization to active generation 1, then immediately suspended with `CAPTURE_LAYOUT_UNSUPPORTED` in generation 2.

The native repair maps only a readable MemFd with validated file size, aligned mapping offset and bounded pixel range. The old published component remains identifiable and is never modified in place.

## Verification
### Regression And Installed Libraries

Nineteen focused Python checks cover metadata, damage continuity, padded pixels, non-page-aligned MemFd offsets, read-only access, mapping reuse/removal, changed buffer identity, invalid/truncated backing files and idempotent stream cleanup.

The complete release gate remains failed, so these results do not certify the full release qualification matrix.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Verified Deployment And Desktop
The earlier accepted v0.22.6 build used clean source `6caee6df1da1` and native Floeterm. An initial older-v0.22.2 deployment failed before text input and was replaced only in the task Runtime; retain that failure with its original version.

No independent virtual desktop was substituted.

## Product Interaction
The task uses an isolated Runtime on port 24864, private state and an authenticated SSH forward.

This qualifies physical playback for that Linux-to-Mac path; destination-clock progress alone is not acoustic proof or a calibrated latency measurement.

## Desktop Launcher Admission Regression
On 2026-10-03, the real Desktop launcher exposed a product contract bug: desktop session `target_url` included `/_redeven_desktop/`, while Desktop window admission requires the registered loopback origin.

The fix returns the port-forward service's canonical origin, retains Desktop's strict validation, preserves IPC rejection diagnostics and removes misleading host-confirmation guidance after a failed launch.

The already-running user Runtime and Desktop were not restarted or replaced.

## Performance And Diagnostics
Each reported product scroll cell ran at least 60 seconds. The first cell failed the unchanged FPS threshold, so the matrix stopped and retained its failure; three passing repetitions and window-motion qualification were not obtained.

| Captured size | Actual painted FPS | Interval P95 | Refinement | Bandwidth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1920x1080 | 36.539 | 31.6ms | 234.4ms | 3.257Mbps |
| 1920x1440 | 39.647 | 33.5ms | 253.9ms | 3.611Mbps |

An unconstrained direct-caps diagnostic first failed with `target not found` and zero frames; the constrained diagnostic and failure are retained separately.

## Authorized Virtual Graphics Comparison
The user explicitly approved provisioning the hypervisor's GL/EGL/Mesa userspace dependencies and normally shutting down and starting only VM 106.

| Capture | Painted FPS | Interval P95 | Refinement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1920x1080 | 26.430 | 51.4ms | 387.5ms |
| 2560x1440 | 22.139 | 58.7ms | 334.9ms |

Raw 1080p capture without conversion or encoding was 32.26 FPS with the console open and 32.91 FPS after the user closed noVNC.

Direct DMA_DRM and linear BGRx DMA-BUF diagnostics failed format negotiation and produced no frames; no production fallback was added.

## Published v0.22.7 Follow-up
Clean Redeven source `69cd04988970c8b456f751838523e61625531d3c` uses the official v0.22.7 module and Linux component digest `09bfc6f9061997c43166ff7810092bf5e79ffaac0112d14a0a0711808e1709bc`.

Preserve the failure; the passing retry alone does not establish its cause.

| Capture | Painted FPS | Interval P95 | Refinement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1920x1080 | 27.458 | 47.1ms | 303.7ms |
| 2560x1440 | 23.458 | 57.1ms | 335.1ms |

frontmatter.title: CI and release gates

concepts.summary:
Redeven uses focused checks during implementation, a fast staged pre-commit
gate, and one complete integration gate for the exact main tip being pushed.
Published dependency evidence, generated assets, localized public docs, UI
behavior, Desktop/runtime bundles, Go tests, lint, and OKF must all agree. A
missing, stale, unsigned, optional, or target-mismatched ReDevPlugin artifact
fails release packaging.
Windows is an internal certification target only; the formal release inventory
fails closed if any Windows asset appears.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
The [self-contained installer distribution](self-contained-installer.md) contract owns prebuilt installer pins, complete suite activation, and the separate guarded default-version promotion after immutable asset publication.

## Validation levels
`AGENTS.md` owns concise global working rules and Git discipline, with an OKF index entrypoint for consultation when additional context is needed.

Redeven native sources and other build output remain scanned; upstream fixture literals must not require disabling a rule for product code.

Workflow cleanup may unregister only its temporary test distributions; product code never performs that system operation.

## Documentation and generated assets
`README.md` is canonical.

Env App builds continue to verify committed assets with `--check`.

## Focused release contracts
The published ReDevPlugin artifact and plugin surface contracts are maintained as focused concepts so this gate remains the owner of exact-main validation order and evidence handoff:

- [ReDevPlugin release artifact gate](redevplugin-release-gates.md) owns upstream publication, runtime evidence, native packaging, and collector inventory. - [Plugin integration gate](plugin-integration-gates.md) owns Host/market/plugin UI integration and its isolated renderer and Desktop smokes.

## Desktop update publication
The protected `redeven-release` environment supplies Developer ID signing, notarization, Sparkle Ed25519, and expected Team ID secrets without committing their values. The hosted Desktop job submits that exact disk image to Apple, requires an `Accepted` result within its bounded wait, and staples and validates its ticket before installer receipts or Sparkle metadata are generated.

Appcasts, signed notes, Linux metadata, and installers are included in the aggregate checksum and remote readback comparison before publication.

## Flower storage compatibility
The [historical writer contract](../ai/flower-upgrade-compatibility.md) is part of every final main integration, including Floret dependency upgrades. Failure and restore tests cover WAL, cross-owner retry, zero execution during preparation, backup protection, full-set replacement interruption and stale outbox rejection.

## Other published boundaries
Floret follows the same published-dependency discipline. Gateway protocol drift fails before packaging.

Workbench PDF drag tests remove only the Vitest runner's outer preview scaling while preserving the product canvas projection, then restore the runner styles after the interaction.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Trust and failure boundaries
The original HTTPS script is the initial trust boundary.

TUF requests preserve cancellation, use bounded HTTP timeouts and do not write the user's trust cache.

Explicit versions can request a rollback.

## Installation transaction
A no-follow, nonblocking lock serializes an activation root. Product-selected regular archive members are closed and bounded; links, duplicates, traversal, unexpected files, missing components, invalid trailers and changed bytes fail.

Upgrade mode does not edit shell profiles, start services or restart Runtime; Runtime owns maintenance and re-exec after installer success.

## Publication and entry cutover
From `v0.13.13`, the authenticated `redeven-installer-contract.json` declares the minimum installer, closed targets and Runtime archive contract. Older installers must stop before acquiring a new incompatible payload.

Installation, historical upgrade and lifecycle qualification remain separate from a successful metadata readiness check.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Upstream publication
The template repository's configured release sources select the official npm `latest` dist-tag and reviewed canonical OCI tags. The catalog is published with a new immutable module tag after isolated generation, Registry preflight, generated-contract verification, SDK acquisition tests, and all upstream Go tests, including the complete frozen historical-format fixtures.

## Published dependency adoption
Redeven queries only `github.com/floegence/redeven-service-templates` through `https://proxy.golang.org` and `sum.golang.org`. The chosen module and go.mod hashes must match the exact go.sum entries.

Maintained knowledge describes stable boundaries and does not need a prose rewrite for each version number.

## Main integration and recovery
Immediately before integration the watcher fetches remote main and compares it with the recorded base.

A failed gate can leave a candidate on the ephemeral runner's local main, but it is never published. Each run removes only its own temporary worktree and private branch.

The [Managed Service release contract](../architecture/managed-service-release-discovery.md) owns installed release identity and user-selected upgrades; catalog adoption does not rebuild, restart, or upgrade installed instances.

frontmatter.title: Local UI certificates

concepts.summary: Runtime owns the saved HTTPS identity and validates it before serving. Desktop exposes explicit certificate creation, import, regeneration, and removal only through the registered management channel. Certificate validity, client trust, and the latest operation result are independent. No operation silently replaces an identity or installs trust. Invalid imports preserve the saved pair; changes affect the next HTTPS start while the running identity and sessions remain intact. HTTP remains the default and requires no certificate.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identity and trust
The user explicitly creates a device CA with `local-authority device-ca generate` and inspects it with `status`. Runtime startup never generates, replaces, or repairs certificate material.

Public export contains certificate material only, never the key.

## Explicit certificate changes
`import`, `regenerate`, and `remove` require `--confirm`. Reject malformed or extraneous PEM blocks, trailing text, encrypted/mismatched keys, invalid dates, invalid chains, missing SANs, and certificates unsuitable for server authentication.

This supports process-interruption recovery; it does not promise an OS trust rollback or filesystem power-loss durability.

## Coverage during network changes
[Local UI network exposure](local-ui-network-exposure.md) owns the two-second interface refresh and atomic public snapshot.

A signing failure retains only current addresses covered by the previous valid leaf and reports `certificate_refresh_failed`; retries recover automatically. Startup and explicit saved-identity preflight retain their strict validation boundary.

## Desktop interaction and private input
The compact HTTPS panel presents certificate validity, expiry, and system trust separately. Public path, fingerprint, and bounded selectable diagnostics live in the expandable details section.

Saving next-start HTTPS settings remains possible with an unusable certificate, with an explicit startup warning.

sections.body: Runtime owns saved identity validation and replacement; Desktop owns explicit management presentation and private file acquisition. Certificate operations cannot silently restart Runtime, install system-wide trust, or expose private material to the renderer.

frontmatter.title: Local UI network exposure

concepts.summary: Runtime owns a public client endpoint independently of the Desktop that starts it. New environments explicitly use HTTP on `localhost:23998`; HTTP needs no certificate. Network exposure retains local browser access and adds reachable network addresses; it requires a fixed port and an effective environment password. HTTPS is an independent explicit choice, with strict certificate validation and client trust. Pages and Flowersec WS/WSS share one public port. A TLS failure never downgrades to HTTP, and the authenticated private Desktop bridge never becomes a public fallback.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## HTTPS certificate ownership
[Local UI certificates](local-ui-certificates.md) owns creation, import, replacement, removal, validation, and client trust. It never creates or repairs certificate material, installs trust, or falls back to HTTP. Certificate replacement affects the next start; the running TLS identity and sessions remain intact.

## Listener and origin boundary
The public listener accepts only canonical authorities derived from its actual bound addresses.

Its isolated `flowersec-private-loopback/1` profile is unchanged and cannot authorize public clients.

## Native Desktop default-port recovery
Only native Desktop launches with saved default `localhost:23998` and no explicit one-start bind override opt in through `--local-ui-default-port-fallback`. Other errors, custom ports, numeric loopback overrides, network binds, and wildcard binds never silently select another port.

External bookmarks containing the old fixed port cannot follow the temporary address.

## Network changes and current reports
While network exposure is enabled, Runtime enumerates eligible interfaces every two seconds. Its public list is explicit, including `[]`; private bridge endpoints cannot supply missing public addresses.

Address failures affect public availability and never assert that the Runtime process has stopped or expose private management URLs.

## Admission and lifecycle
A network listener starts only for a concrete non-loopback IP or wildcard with a fixed nonzero port and an effective password.

Occupied explicit ports fail with a startup error instead of silently selecting another port.

Flowersec owns admission, session establishment, liveness, handler dispatch, close, and lease release; Redeven does not copy those loops.

## Server-owned access configuration
[Runtime two-factor authentication](runtime-two-factor-authentication.md) owns the persistent credential authority, one-time bcrypt verifier migration, TOTP enrollment, recovery, replay protection, and ordinary-session revocation. Explicit password changes remain next-start settings when MFA is disabled; MFA-enabled settings cannot clear/replace that password or downgrade HTTPS.

Failed catalog saves roll back verifier initialization as well as replacement and clearing.

concepts.summary:
Redeven supplies authenticated host facts and source policy to ReDevPlugin; it
does not accept plugin ownership, authority, provenance, or trust from browser
payloads. Every HTTP route passes explicit authentication, origin, CSRF, and
closed-action authorization, and direct Host calls pass the same owner/action/
resource policy. External package source, signature, execution approval, update

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Local process boundary
The `process.local` permission is an explicit high-risk grant and method-level Process Broker access is checked again for every Worker invocation. The Host does not inherit the complete Redeven environment and never injects session cookies, plugin tokens, or Host credentials.

See [Plugin process sessions](../architecture/plugin-process-sessions.md) for the lifecycle contract.

## Authenticated session boundary
The session resolver accepts only a Redeven channel id whose stored metadata has exact non-empty channel, user, and environment identities.

The bounded session cache is keyed by owner-session hash and accepts a hit only when all four hashes match.

Guessed owner sweeps and local teardown registries are prohibited.

## HTTP and direct authorization
The canonical route is `/_redevplugin/api/plugins`.

Method effect is resolved before local policy clamps it, while shared runtime management remains admin-only.

## Permission management projection
Plugin Center reads active grants and explicit plugin security policies through released ReDevPlugin APIs. It never writes registry tables, invents a default grant for a catalog plugin, or treats catalog identity as permission.

Its actual trust badge remains unchanged; only verified catalog trust may receive the `Official` trust badge.

## Package admission and trust
The retained release install/update path accepts only the exact source policy, revocation evidence, publisher, plugin, version, signed release metadata, package hashes, and Host requirement. Browser-supplied trust state, arbitrary package bytes, rollback, unknown publishers, invalid or revoked signatures, and invented fetch provenance are denied.

Redeven does not add a new authorization workflow; the existing official release-ref verification remains unchanged.

## Capability confirmation plans
ReDevPlugin validates a capability preflight result against the Host-known capability response schema before it becomes a confirmation plan. Values in the reserved `redevplugin.capability.risk_plan.*` namespace must match the strict v1 risk-plan contract; an unknown or malformed reserved version fails closed instead of falling back to a generic object.

Replacing or replaying any of those values requires a new confirmation.

## Runtime trust
Runtime descriptors bind version, target, IPC, WASM ABI, and artifact hash. Darwin release bytes receive their Developer ID signature before the product digest and Sigstore evidence, and later Desktop signing must preserve that exact nested executable. Startup must not hash the field binary and accept that value as its own trust anchor.

## Business adapter and observability boundary
Plugin business adapters are invoked only after ReDevPlugin resolves lifecycle, permission, confirmation, lease, quota, revocation, and audit context. Product code cannot bypass that chain.

Raw adapter errors, tokens, secrets, cookies, query strings, absolute paths, and complete URLs are not copied into public or durable diagnostic detail.

sections.title: Boundaries

Desktop runtime-control tokens, direct-session artifacts, Gateway credentials, RCPP credentials, and Flower grants are not plugin ambient authority.

Redeven security adapters may narrow authority; they may not mint platform tokens, weaken route policy, edit opaque state, or replace released brokers.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Session authority and lifetime
The gate alone decides channel authorization when registering the channel and its lifetime cancellation callback under one lock. Callers supply verified private-management identity or an ordinary login session ID, never an `unlocked` assertion.

Runtime restart clears in-memory sessions and incomplete operations; it preserves committed authentication state.

## Browser Cookie scope and continuity
Local UI alone issues, reads and clears `redeven_local_access_<http|https>_<port>`. Forwarded headers cannot select the scope.

Only an incorrect password or factor produces input validation feedback; transport failures and cooldowns retain their own messages.

## Desktop consumption and forwarding
Desktop Flower retains the complete Runtime-issued access-cookie `name=value` pair and returns it unchanged. It never derives the name from a bridge or forwarded client port.

No upstream platform capability changes are required for this product authentication policy.

frontmatter.title: Runtime two-factor authentication

concepts.summary: Runtime `accessgate` owns environment authentication independently of Redeven Cloud. Enabling two-factor authentication requires the environment password followed by a TOTP or single-use recovery code for ordinary browser, direct URL, and Cloud data sessions. A password-only challenge grants no file, terminal, editor, plugin, or forwarding access. Authenticated native/SSH management retains its separate private host authority; loopback addresses, Cloud administrator claims, and forwarded headers do not establish that authority. Missing or damaged committed authentication state fails closed. Host recovery locks ordinary access until a new password and authenticator are committed.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Enrollment and management
Desktop Environment Settings / Access presents one two-factor row. If a different environment password has been saved for the next start, restart before configuring MFA; the old running verifier cannot overwrite the newer saved authority.

These commands do not alter SSH keys, sshd policy, PAM, host passwords, or execution identity.

## Session authority
[Runtime access sessions](runtime-access-sessions.md) owns ordinary session deadlines, browser Cookie scope and refresh continuity, challenge binding, native editor delegation, and revocation. MFA management changes revoke ordinary authority through that single gate; they do not create a second browser or Desktop authentication lifecycle.

## Persistence, replay and recovery
`access-auth.sqlite` is a versioned, private SQLite authority, separate from the transport authorization database. The committed database and initialized key become the sole authority; deletion, malformed data, unsafe modes, symlinks, unknown schema, or key loss cannot fall back to the retired verifier.

Authentication state and secrets are not diagnostic export inputs.

Only plugin instance, plugin, and surface identifiers are persisted. Execution plans, admission credentials, temporary URLs, and management revisions are resolved through the current plugin opening flow and never saved in navigation.

Loading and cache authority follow [Env App resource snapshots](env-resource-cache.md).

concepts.summary:
Redeven chooses interaction mode through released Floe layout configuration.
Native Desktop always uses desktop interaction. Browser mobile interaction
requires all three conditions: width below 768 CSS pixels, a coarse primary
pointer, and no primary hover capability. Narrow mouse windows retain Activity
and Workbench. Floe owns media-query observation, local space measurement, and
drawer placement/focus; Redeven owns navigation disclosure and content.
Automatic sidebar placement never changes saved navigation or collapse preferences.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## One interaction mode
Desktop Welcome and Desktop-hosted Env App configure `mobileQuery: 'not all'`; the Env App recognizes its native host through the existing Desktop bridge.

Resizing a desktop browser cannot rewrite its saved Activity/Workbench choice or activate mobile terminal input.

A hidden toolbar action must retain an explicit reachable entry.

## Temporary desktop navigation
Shell, Flower conversations, Files/Git navigation, and Terminal sessions measure their own shared navigation/content region. When that region cannot fit the current sidebar width plus 480 CSS pixels of main content, the sidebar becomes a transient left side drawer.

Mobile navigation retains its product-specific bottom/side panel behavior under the [mobile Shell](mobile-shell-navigation.md) and [Flower](flower-mobile-navigation.md) contracts.

Desktop Flower retains its mark, title, introduction, working directory, four complete starter suggestions, and keyboard hints even when the chat region is 767 CSS pixels or narrower. Container queries adjust spacing and the suggestion grid; they cannot hide content or switch interaction mode.

Narrow layouts may ellipsize selection titles; explanations remain normal prose and mobile suggestion cards retain their compact presentation.

frontmatter.description: One product-owned stacking contract orders movable windows, Flower, plugin surfaces, blocking modals, and command UI.
frontmatter.title: Env App floating layer order

concepts.summary:
Env App owns one global stacking contract for cross-surface UI. Movable product and plugin windows share a most-recently-used band from 1000 through 1099; the expanded Flower companion is 2000, its context previews use 2100 through 2199, the plugin launcher Panel is 3000, blocking product modals are 4000, and the command palette is 5000. No surface may escape its assigned band through an ad hoc `z-index`. A window interaction changes only the movable-window order, while higher product layers remain stable and operable.

Published Floe Webapp constrains dialogs and floating windows to the visible
viewport or owning projected surface. Toolbar and keyboard changes preserve
reachable window controls and local content scrolling; temporary bounds do not
replace the live preferred geometry.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Drag-region synchronization
Desktop's embedded host projects iframe-relative native drag regions. A settled snapshot must not schedule another animation frame by rebuilding itself.

Native pointer and floating geometry ownership remain upstream.

## Global bands
The command palette is always the top Env App surface at 5000.

Window-local menus, tooltips, and recovery panels must not cross a global band.

## Dialog placement
Mobile plugin and tools navigation is local to the released Shell content region, not a global launcher modal.

Clicking the backdrop closes only the Dialog; the first click never reaches the Activity content beneath it.

Interactive titlebar controls retain their existing no-drag exclusions.

## Visible viewport boundaries
Published Floe Webapp owns the visible viewport, safe areas, Safari fixed-origin conversion, and projected surface intersection for Dialog and FloatingWindow. Product CSS must not bypass this boundary with fixed panel positions, viewport-unit heights plus removed maximums, or forced transforms.

Temporary viewport constraints do not replace upstream's live preferred window size.

## Movable window order
One Shell-lifetime provider registers every open movable window under a stable identifier.

It never uses an unbounded incrementing counter, stays inside 1000–1099 for ordinary windows or 2100–2199 for Flower context previews, and keeps a multiply registered identifier until all owners unregister. The minimized Debug Console entry is a launcher control at the base of the window band rather than an open movable window.

## Flower dismissal
The Flower companion remains above ordinary movable windows while expanded; its owned context preview remains above it and below plugin Panels and product modals. It must not return focus to the retained composer because composer focus is an expansion intent. Activity plugin window interaction is also outside Flower: host pointer or focus input and trusted plugin bridge activation, focus, or action events collapse the companion without consuming the destination interaction, including when the event originates inside a cross-origin iframe and cannot bubble through the product document.

sections.title: Contract

The Shell requests `GET /_redeven_proxy/api/ui-cache-scope` as soon as an authenticated connection is available, in parallel with current-session read permission confirmation. The value is not a credential and cannot select request authority.

Container projections follow that same owner instead of clearing their inventory on connection changes.

## Persistence and presentation
Browser clients use Floe's asynchronous IndexedDB adapter. Cache files never enter synchronous UI preferences.

Activating a Codespaces view refreshes its shared inventory; no new polling or connection recovery loop is introduced.

## Actions and recovery
A stale application is resolved through current inventory before launch.

Cached restoration never installs components, requests permissions, launches processes, or starts lifecycle operations.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Page rendering
Files ending in `.html`, `.htm`, or `.xhtml`, regardless of case, open as rendered pages in floating windows, mobile previews, Workbench, and attachment snapshot previews.

It renders an opaque `allow-scripts`, no-referrer iframe; it never inserts file HTML into the trusted shell or navigates to an authenticated file endpoint.

The current Activity file preview and Workbench same-file reuse rules still own placement.

## Placement and interaction
The page fills the reading area and scrolls internally. An unselected Workbench iframe is inert and cannot intercept pointer, keyboard, or wheel input. Unrelated shell updates preserve the live document.

## Source editing and snapshots
Edit opens the existing HTML source editor only when write permission permits. Attachment snapshots remain read-only and show the attached bytes rather than re-reading the live file.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Window boundary
The [floating layer contract](env-app-floating-layer-order.md) owns window placement and visible viewport constraints. The preview title, close action and document toolbar remain reachable while the document scrolls in its own reading area.

## Reading area and zoom
Sizing uses local CSS pixels, excluding padding and scrollbars. Ancestor CSS transforms, including Workbench projection, must not change intrinsic document size.

Flower attachment windows retain native browser PDF controls and image containment; their document containers must shrink with the window.

## Rendering ownership
PDF uses the lazy published `@floegence/floe-webapp-core/pdf` entrypoint. Its scoped CSS must not affect unrelated surfaces.

Image load and error callbacks must match the currently displayed resource.

## HTML pages
The [HTML file preview contract](file-preview-html.md) owns page-first opening, source editing, bounded content, and isolated document interaction.

## Markdown enhancements
Mermaid processing checks for diagram elements before resolving theme colors or allocating a rendering sandbox. Diagram rendering retains theme-specific caching and rejects stale document work.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Title bar and reading space
The desktop preview passes its actions through `FloatingWindow.headerActions` using the product's `PreviewWindow` and `PersistentFloatingWindow` adapters.

Copying still copies the complete path and briefly confirms success even though the path is no longer displayed in the floating window.

## Workbench reading space and narrow widgets
Workbench shows the file name in its existing header and exposes the full path through the title tooltip and copy action. Its body starts directly below the header, except when an existing pending-sync notice is present.

Keyboard navigation, Escape/Tab dismissal, and focus restoration must not activate canvas gestures or reclaim focus through the widget shell.

## One action implementation
`FilePreviewActions` owns action presentation and temporary copy feedback.

Header button input must preserve the selected reading text. Downloads keep the current file and draft mapping owned by the product download command builder.

## PDF drafts and persistence
Writable PDFs expose the existing Edit file action. PDF.js saves full Unicode field values, but when the original field font cannot encode them, it sets `NeedAppearances` instead of embedding a replacement form font.

No browser-only blob download bypasses the product download manager.

## Unavailable targets and recovery
Navigation opens the current filesystem object, while historical tool results, diffs, and image snapshots retain their original content. A target that fails after opening uses a compact panel with Retry and Open parent folder.

Preview dismissal and resource lifetime follow the [file preview dismissal contract](file-preview-dismissal.md).

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Preview loading and error presentation remain in the body. A title-bar layout change must not add a second close policy or bypass discard confirmation.

Preview scale, content bounds, and asynchronous renderer ownership follow the [viewport and rendering contract](file-preview-viewport-and-rendering.md).

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Close and reopen
Explicit close clears the controller request immediately so the browser is no longer active and focus restoration can proceed.

The same FloatingWindow owner cancels a pending exit; an earlier close completion must not retire the reopened surface.

Closing must not leave an independent timeout or detached browser alive after the window disappears.

## Responsiveness and resource lifetime
Closing must accept subsequent page actions without waiting for exit motion. The focused browser fixture exercises 1,000 directory entries and five cycles, checks synchronous close and frame intervals below 50ms, and verifies that controller close, opener focus, and an underlying action remain responsive.

concepts.summary:
Published Floe Webapp owns directory navigation, validation state, and asynchronous
request lifetime. Redeven supplies the target runtime connection, authoritative
path context, localized copy, and product form state. All picker paths are
absolute; `/` always means the target environment's filesystem root. Home and
Root are navigation shortcuts and cannot grant access. Failed navigation retains

The runtime revalidates every create or execution request against current policy.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Absolute paths and runtime authority
DirectoryPicker, DirectoryInput, and file pickers consume the same released navigation core. A failed or malformed context cannot be replaced by synthesized Home or Root permissions.

Session, filesystem, OS, and process authorization remain governed by [permission policy and filesystem scope](../security/permission-policy-and-filesystem-scope.md).

## Navigation state and failures
Every mounted picker owns its current directory, loaded entries, path input, hidden-item switch, and validity.

Earlier successes or failures cannot overwrite newer input, navigation, error, or selection state.

A cached or previously validated selection is never an authorization token: creation and later operations can fail if policy, filesystem contents, or OS permissions change.

## Live language changes
Host-supplied Home and Root labels resolve through the active locale accessor. The change retains the current path, input element, pending selection, composer draft, and runtime authorization; it never reloads context solely to translate a label. Both Desktop Flower and Env App use this shared product adapter.

## Product presentations
Files uses the same released `parsePickerPath` and `formatPickerPath` functions for its path editor. An entered `/...` path never acquires a Home prefix, regardless of the currently selected root.

Its actual scroll viewports carry Workbench local-scroll markers; existing modal, keyboard, and focus ownership remains with the host and published presentation components.

## Shared directory favorites
All Env App and Desktop directory and file pickers receive the published controlled favorites contract. Shortcut views cannot confirm an earlier selected directory.

See [directory favorites](directory-favorites.md) for authentication, persistence, refresh and failure contracts.

concepts.summary: After access first becomes ready, Env App owns one stable `EnvAIPage` and `FlowerSurface`. On desktop, the published `BottomBarCompanion` provides a centered collapsed field and a bounded detail surface that grows upward without changing body geometry. The dedicated Activity Bar page and an available, unfiltered Workbench Flower widget are placements of that same product tree. Workbench selection controls canvas input and focus only; clearing selection never revokes Flower placement or engagement. Placement changes hosts, presentation, visibility, and engagement; it never creates a second Flower surface or changes Floret authority. Floret owns thread lifecycle state, while Redeven owns product placement, read acknowledgement, and ephemeral UI state.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Companion ownership
`@floegence/floe-webapp-core/layout` owns the reusable companion shell, fixed geometry, visual-viewport and safe-area clamping, motion phases, capture-phase outside dismissal, Escape routing, and explicit mount handling.

The companion Portal mounts to the explicit Activity overlay host and never falls back to `document.body`.

A running task never prevents the user from collapsing the companion or clicking another surface.

## Activity Terminal footer
Desktop Activity Terminal registers a 24-pixel anchor in its existing 28-pixel footer, centered in the terminal content column with a maximum width of 360 pixels and room to shrink.

Workbench Terminal widgets and mobile terminals never register an entry; their existing footer heights and navigation remain unchanged. This placement does not introduce a second Flower instance, change terminal transport, or route Flower keystrokes through terminal input.

## Stable Flower placement
The product root consumes the same authoritative visibility decision for native `hidden`, `aria-hidden`, and `inert`.

[Flower setup and settings](flower-setup-and-settings.md#retained-panels) owns retained form, editor and inactive-panel semantics.

## Contextual Ask Flower
New companion conversations can include the desktop Activity origin page through the read-only page reader selected by Shell's current Activity ID.

Send and context-action behavior remain defined by [Flower turn launcher](flower-turn-launcher.md).

## Presence and summary
[Flower companion presence](flower-companion-presence.md) owns collapsed status priority, live output tails, completion acknowledgement, composer precedence, and the single workspace observation stream. Presence never changes the placement and focus ownership defined here.

## Dismissal, focus, and reads
Capture-phase outside pointer dismissal includes the companion shell, its anchor, and explicitly classified Flower-owned Portal surfaces. Activity plugin windows project host pointer and focus input plus trusted iframe bridge activation, focus, and action events into the same outside-dismiss behavior, because cross-origin iframe events cannot bubble into the product document.

Shared SSE summaries remain activity-only, while initial/reconnect baselines and later viewer read-state envelopes are scoped to the same `UserPublicID`.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
The Workbench Flower widget retains its existing window, canvas, and focus contracts while contributing only a placement host for the Env App-owned Flower product.

The companion never auto-expands for completion, failure, approval, or user input. Showing an available, unfiltered Workbench Flower widget moves the retained product tree into that widget without starting a second list load or live stream, and later canvas deselection does not move it away.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Stable disclosure and safe content
Activity identity uses thread, run, turn, and canonical item ID.

Consecutive tools and bounded thinking use [tool sequences](flower-tool-sequences.md) for compact spacing and group disclosure, without replacing individual details.

## Thread query and read details
`Thread Query:` and `Thread Read:` are fixed English technical tool labels; their suffix preserves the model-authored invocation intent in the user's language. See the [thread query contract](../ai/flower-thread-queries.md) for canonical lookup, privacy, server bounds and failure behavior.

## Web search details
Web operations use one localized action title for visible and accessible labels.

Expanded details contain only actual per-call results and errors, never the header's query, URL, pattern or status.

Floret v7.44.1 preserves URL-only sources through validation and canonical restart.

## Semantic tool icons
Collapsed rows retain their compact geometry. Each registered tool, the hosted web-search activity, source activity, MCP extension, and unknown extension has an explicit type glyph.

Both Desktop and Env App consume the same component.

## Intent, inputs and results
The collapsed title describes the invocation intent. Actual outcomes never replace the invocation intent.

Presentation never supplies execution input or authorization.

## Viewport and gesture ownership
One controller per viewport owns transcript position. Layout, focus, animation and growth never resume a reading pause.

Hidden controls do not enter the focus or hit-test order.

## Visual motion
The disclosure motion owner uses one current Web Animation: opening takes 180 ms and closing takes 140 ms. Reversal cancels the prior animation, and its obsolete completion cannot change presence.

[SubAgent detail](flower-subagent-detail.md) owns child grouping and projection; its viewport controller cannot affect the parent transcript.

sections.title: Contract

## Reading and layout
Approval uses one keyed flat list for both single and multiple actions. Each row pairs its safe operation label with independent Floe Reject and Allow once capsules; risk, actual file/network targets, and unavailable reasons remain visible.

After an input response advances to approval, the existing focus handoff prefers the first enabled decision and falls back to Stop when no decision is available.

## Canonical decisions and drafts
Every pending, requested primary approval remains visible even when its action reports `can_approve=false`, the adapter cannot mutate, the selected thread is read-only, or detail is pending; those states disable every decision action and present the canonical unavailable or read-only reason instead of falling back to chat.

No local handoff, consumed-interaction set, approval generation, or command busy reducer controls canonical visibility.

## Safe presentation
One pure presenter owns operation classification, title, description, command, targets, and risk. Operation fallbacks are independent localized strings and never extracted from translated sentences. Internal tool names and target-encoding prefixes are never user-facing.

concepts.summary:
- Authority: published Floret v7.32.0 assistant messages own durable sources; Flower reads current views and historical pages through the existing thread projection.
- Outcome: provider citation markers in prose become readable links with source titles. Copying a message removes those markers.
- Invariants: ranges use end-exclusive Unicode code-point indices in the exact assistant text. URLs must be HTTP(S), without credentials, whitespace or control characters. Marker identifiers never establish a URL.
- Failure boundary: unmatched sources appear at the end of the completed message. Historical provider markers without stored sources show localized unavailable text; Flower never reconstructs missing provider facts. Explicit Markdown bibliographies remain authored content.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Provider annotations preserve title, URL and optional positions through the model gateway and Floret provider adapter. Floret validates sources, binds them to canonical assistant fragments and supplies the same facts in current and detail projections.

Invalid URLs never become links, and metadata changes invalidate Markdown HTML without remounting stable code controls.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
The published Floe Webapp v0.86.32 `createMarkdownParser` owns GFM syntax with CJK-aware emphasis boundaries for completed and streamed text. Display parsing never writes back to canonical messages or provider cache input. New messages preserve complete sources; old records lacking sources remain readable without rewriting historical data.

## Inline-code references
Inline Markdown code derives from the published Floe `--inline-code-foreground` and `--inline-code-background` pair.

Fenced code, copy behavior and canonical content remain independent.

Theme changes preserve focus, selection, DOM and geometry; see [message appearance](flower-message-appearance.md).

## Source-card presentation
Sources start collapsed, showing the count and a deduplicated stack of up to four website icons plus an overflow count. Sources never expose their own copy button. Inline citations retain their existing links.

## Website icons
The shared Flower UI bundles 27 common website marks from pinned theSVG assets with audited per-icon licenses. Icon enhancement runs independently after Markdown rendering; collapse/expand never restarts it.

The renderer receives image bytes, never a third-party tracking URL.

## Authored bibliography
Assistant Markdown can already contain an explicit bibliography inside an unlabelled, `text` or `plaintext` fence. This is display-only authored content: it neither fabricates canonical source annotations nor binds numeric prose references to provider metadata. User messages and fetched external Markdown do not enable this assistant-specific presentation.

## Stable content boundary
Flower decorates only regions changed by the published incremental parser.

Finalization only finishes unfinished decoration: it never releases an already settled code block, recreates its copy icons, resubmits Worker work or replaces a protected selection.

HTML preview fences retain the existing media contract.

Use frozen, published dependencies in both hosts.

Timing is evidence for the bounded fixture, not a guarantee for unlimited input.

```bash bash scripts/check_desktop_electron_test_runtime.sh desktop node scripts/check_flower_code_highlighting.mjs --output=/tmp/flower-code-highlighting ```

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
## Interaction and cost

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Status and live output
Floating companion presence is a pure canonical summary projection with active work first: running, queued, attention, unread failure, unread canceled, unread completed, unavailable, idle.

Reduced motion disables flow, transition tracking, and arrival motion while retaining semantic color and text.

## Completion acknowledgement
A successful transition for a run that the collapsed companion previously observed as running may temporarily replace the idle composer with one localized completion acknowledgement. This is ephemeral product feedback, not canonical completed presence: initial history, queued-only work, failures, cancellations, attention, mismatched or expired runs, and completion while any running or queued work remains never trigger it. Historical completion remains forbidden from the collapsed companion.

## Observation and transport
The companion consumes the same single workspace SSE as the full Flower surface. Shared summaries never manufacture personal read state.

Expansion keeps the same connection and requests the selected thread current view rather than creating a second stream.

## Composer precedence
One derived entry description owns collapsed rendering and target identity.

- The current thread's pending decision entry, regardless of question kind, selected option, custom-answer mode, or draft content. - The ordinary chat editor when a draft, attachment, reference, focus, or IME session is present; an enabled inspection entry preserves access if editing is unavailable. - An eligible running, queued, unread-failure, or ephemeral-completion status button with its exact target thread. - The ordinary editor, or an inspection entry for a read-only or unavailable editor.

[Flower Activity companion](flower-activity-companion.md) owns public question copy, activation, and one-shot focus handoffs.

sections.title: Contract

An attachment selected while the model capability snapshot is loading stays queued with its local bytes.

Attachment-only turns are valid and never receive invented prompt copy.

No automatic Send occurs during restoration.

## Connection-local editing
Activity and Workbench use one Env App shell-owned in-memory coordinator; Desktop uses one App-owned coordinator per connection. A Flower surface never creates a module singleton.

Admission uncertainty preserves that product request identity in the live connection so retry and reconciliation cannot silently create another request.

## Queued content
Active execution keeps file selection, paste, drag-and-drop and reference controls available. Users can remove or add resources and send normally; staged copies remain usable after the queue item is removed, while canonical attachment bytes stay immutable.

## Canonical Presentation
Message attachment previews cross the host's authenticated `loadMessageAttachment` boundary. Env App prepares its local access credentials; Desktop sends a scoped GET through Runtime IPC and receives bounded bytes with the canonical MIME type.

A real Chromium 320-CSS-pixel layout check covers common desktop 400-percent zoom width without horizontal overflow.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Ask Flower context
The shared launcher and embedded Tessiven composer show linked context inside their existing composite input boundary.

Chips sit side by side, wrap and scroll inside a bounded input region under the host's existing local-scroll contract.

Editable `@` references keep their existing controls.

## Composer interaction
The full composer recognizes an editable `@` token only at a whitespace boundary with a collapsed caret.

Composer focus preserves the same one-pixel geometry and shadow, changing only to a restrained border color; candidate and directory-action focus-visible states remain explicit.

## New conversation origin page
[Activity origin page references](flower-page-context.md) owns opening/New capture, authorized page readers, layout scope and removal. Host snapshot presentation is injected without transferring draft or canonical-reference authority; Env App reuses the right-click Ask Flower preview window and text viewer for both editable and submitted snapshots.

## Conversation references
[Conversation reference interaction](flower-thread-references.md) owns frozen basic snapshots, menu entry points, preview, removal and submission recovery. The same draft owner and type dispatch support thread, page and file references.

## Bounded discovery
Discovery searches the current thread's immutable working directory or the new-thread working-directory draft.

A token without a slash uses that bounded global matching behavior. Root read errors are visible and retryable; inaccessible descendants are skipped within the same bounded scan.

## Draft and admission
The connection-local composer stores ordered file/directory, page-context and thread chips with a product-local identity and host-derived label. This editable draft is never written to Redeven, Floret, local storage, IndexedDB, or another connection.

After admission, the one-pass mapping defined by [AI tool runtime](../ai/ai-tool-runtime.md) gives Floret the canonical ordered `MessageReference` values and turn context snapshots.

## Queue previews and editing
Canonical queue references remain visible as compact icons and use exact ThreadID, QueueID and ReferenceID for file/directory preview. New submission repeats normal authorization and admission; display labels never reconstruct opaque resource authority.

concepts.summary:
Flower remembers explicit choices for future root conversations in one
Redeven-owned product store, scoped by authenticated namespace, endpoint, and
user. The existing controls and layout are unchanged. Loading or switching a
Thread never writes a preference. Existing Threads and immutable Turns keep

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Ownership and persistence
`ai_conversation_preferences` belongs to `ai_threadstore_product_v1`, schema version 11. The v10-to-v11 transactional migration validates both historical and target shapes, preserves product data, and never infers a user's preference from old Threads.

Stable scope absence cannot read another user's defaults.

## Selection events
Only the selected field is patched. Existing-Thread edits must succeed before personal memory is changed; a later memory failure does not roll back the confirmed Thread result.

Explicit Default remains distinct from absent memory; existing Default/budget and Off/budget semantics are unchanged.

## Drafts and admission
Shared drafts separate explicit `model_id_override`/`working_dir_override` from effective `model_id`/`working_dir` admission projections. Old Thread selection cannot seed the new draft.

Existing busy/queued/unresolved-interaction edit restrictions are unchanged.

## Concurrency and failure
Each authenticated adapter orders captured field patches and loads the latest revision before writing. The product store atomically merges fields and uses compare-and-set revision; concurrent stale writes return HTTP 409 and are not automatically retried.

Thread/draft targets and model identities are captured before asynchronous work; a late response cannot retarget another draft or navigate the surface.

sections.body:
## Navigation and presentation
The page has one identity header, a return-to-chat action, and two accessible Skills/MCP tabs with arrow, Home, and End navigation.

Both carriers resolve explicit copy for every shipped locale, including plural counts and locale-aware check timestamps.

Every skill and MCP row reserves a 32px icon beside its name without increasing row height. Icons are decorative, retain the adjacent accessible name, and never become interactive targets or inline untrusted SVG markup.

MCP discovery and persistence follow [the runtime icon contract](../ai/mcp-runtime.md#presentation-icons).

## Skills
Catalog and source metadata load once the connection is usable.

Catalog refresh and mutations are serialized so an older read cannot overwrite a successful change.

Browsing requires read access and never installs bundled files on disk.

## MCP
Add or edit a server using a remote HTTP endpoint or a local executable with one argument per line. Existing secret values are never filled into a form; omission keeps them and an explicit empty object clears them.

Search, enabled filtering, discovered tool details, explicit connection checks, and confirmed removal are available from the MCP tab.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Candidates and ownership
Only canonical ordinary user messages in the selected thread are eligible.

Draft ownership remains defined by [Flower composer references](flower-composer-references.md).

## Keyboard interaction
An exactly empty ordinary chat textarea accepts unmodified ArrowUp to recall the newest eligible input.

A nonempty draft, including whitespace, never starts history browsing.

Changing threads resets navigation while each thread's ordinary draft remains in its existing scope.

Viewer read events and current-only updates cannot manufacture loaded-content coverage.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Transcript reading scale
Assistant and user bubbles share the original `0.875rem` body size and unitless `1.75` line height (14px and 24.5px at the standard 16px root).

Their `1.6` line height keeps wrapped content readable, while the status label uses `0.75rem` with `1.4` line height.

## Assistant reading roles
Assistant body and headings retain the published foreground on the chat surface.

Authored bold text, dates, identifiers, source labels and destinations remain unchanged; presentation does not infer metadata from prose or rewrite admitted Markdown.

## Filled messages and content
Sent user text and answered-question receipts use `selection-bg` and `selection-fg`.

Their text and selection use the inset reading roles so the error background cannot leave selection-colored message text unreadable.

Code retains theme-colored insets; its text derives from the theme foreground with bounded lightness.

## User media and resources
Each submitted user message presents image thumbnails first, then one wrapping row of resource cards, then its text bubble and existing timestamp/copy actions. Resource-only and image-only messages never create an empty text bubble.

Canonical reference previews retain exact thread, turn and reference identity; queued context actions retain their distinct authority and pending-click guard.

## Native text selection
Filled bubble text, including transparent table headers, uses Floe's contrasting `selection-on-primary` pair. Selecting text never changes parsing, content, copy behavior or transport state.

Browser coverage measures actual rendered colors across all 26 published presets and both surface materials. Ordinary and selected message text must reach 4.5:1. Code highlighting retains its independent [stable-content contract](flower-code-highlighting.md).

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
The composer always keeps its model label visible without an availability spinner or busy status.

Runtime status distinguishes no Desktop provider (`not_configured`), configured but unavailable keys or catalog (`missing_keys` or `empty`), and actual connection or protocol errors.

## Model identity and recovery
Thread snapshots, list items, and patches carry `model_id` and `reasoning_selection` as thread defaults. The last is a disabled, ungrouped display of a thread's missing model; Flower never silently replaces it.

See [reasoning selection ownership](flower-reasoning-selection.md) for loading, draft, and submission rules.

## Web search presentation
Model choices display the shared search badge from the server's readonly `web_search` projection. A provider brand or frontend model name never enables search. See [model directory ownership](../ai/model-directory-and-selection.md).

## Permission and navigation
Below the 768px viewport breakpoint, the composer keeps permission status and selection in its own More panel, alongside any other overflow controls.

Saving disables only the permission control, prevents duplicate requests, merges the authoritative settings response, and restores the confirmed value on failure.

Warm sessions switch without provider or transcript remount and stale loads cannot replace the current thread.

The header switcher is only a product-specific compact presentation; it does not create a second selected-thread owner or change the requested, committed, and content-presented ordering.

concepts.summary: Confirmed Thread settings own the reasoning level displayed for an existing Flower conversation. Drafts own only explicit new-thread choices; computed defaults never become draft intent. Default reasoning is a configuration choice, not an enabled state or an effort level. Cold loading and restart preserve explicit Off and On. Controls reflect verified model capabilities; unknown controls remain model-controlled. Failed saves retain the confirmed setting, and active Turns retain their immutable runtime configuration.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Existing Threads display the newest confirmed settings snapshot in `ThreadCache`, comparing settings revisions independently of runtime view versions. Loading, reconnecting, and rendering must never write a reasoning preference.

New-thread Off survives shared-surface remounts and attachment preparation, while changing to a confirmed model without reasoning clears the unsupported draft choice.

[Conversation preferences](flower-conversation-preferences.md) store only explicit reasoning choices, keyed by the complete model identity and including budget tokens. Loading, sending, reconnecting, and automatic model normalization never write preferences. A preference-save failure retains the confirmed Thread result and reports a separate save error; active Turns and retry snapshots remain immutable.

All shared control variants use one ordered option list and localized labels. An explicit `default` is never labeled On or replaced with a specific effort.

The UI does not infer an effective provider default.

The shared Desktop and Env App control distinguishes these model contracts:

| Declared capability | Presentation |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean toggle | Default, Off when supported, and explicit On |
| Named efforts | Default, Off when supported, and only declared supported levels |
| Token budget | Bounded token input; clearing it removes the override |
| Fixed thinking | Non-interactive Always on status |
| Thinking with unknown controls | Non-interactive Model controlled status with an explanation |
| No reasoning | No reasoning control |

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: This is shared Redeven UI policy, not a Floret API or a second preference store. Runtime continuation uses the [immutable Turn surface](../ai/floret-thread-runtime.md); no reasoning override is added to an input answer.

frontmatter.description: First-time model setup, actionable starter tasks, and shared provider, permission, and computer settings.
frontmatter.title: Flower setup and settings

concepts.summary:
The shared Flower surface owns setup and settings for Desktop and Env App.
An empty profile without a usable model or selected conversation offers explicit
setup actions. Configured new conversations offer starter tasks as editable
drafts; selecting one never launches a turn. Settings use flat sections and
preserve drafts, model-source identity and permission ownership. Connection
failures and configured profiles needing repair retain their recovery controls.
Settings open in a shared modal dialog over the mounted chat. Background chat
and navigation stay visible but inert until the dialog finishes closing; covered
chat does not acknowledge reads. Settings save progress and errors survive hiding.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## First-time setup
The welcome replaces disabled suggestions only when no thread is selected, no provider is configured, no model is usable, and the Desktop source is absent, `not_configured`, or `empty`. In a Desktop `local_host` session, the sole destination is the current Flower surface's settings dialog; it must not open or focus another Welcome window or identify the local environment as remote.

The shared icon artwork stays bare, without restoring the removed glow or a continuous animation.

## Starter tasks
The configured new-conversation page offers four everyday tasks: understand the current folder's contents and how to use them, understand the connected computer, discover installed applications, and prepare a folder organization plan.

Matching names or older dates alone never justify deletion.

The compact companion continues to omit the task grid as specified by the [companion presentation contract](flower-activity-companion.md).

## Settings composition
Settings edit the environment profile even with a Desktop model source.

Switch saves are immediate, block duplicate edits, and restore the previous state on failure.

The shared settings panel stays mounted when returning to chat.

## Provider configuration
Provider layout, authentication choices, and connection-before-model sequencing belong to [Flower provider configuration](flower-provider-configuration.md).

## Retained panels
FlowerSurface owns chat and extensions plus one lazily loaded settings form. A bounded, scrollable body adapts to the visible viewport.

Settings dialog interactions belong to the companion; closing the dialog leaves the companion expanded, while the host collapse action closes both without discarding forms.

## Saving and ownership
The adapter exposes independent `saveDefaultPermission`, `saveModelProfile`, and `persistDefaultModel` operations. Default permission uses a serialized 700 ms controller that coalesces rapid changes, protects newer choices from older responses, and restores the last confirmed value on failure. Computer-use save failures restore the confirmed switch and expose the error.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Starter-task selection creates an editable draft, never a turn.

Permission descriptions sit outside the single-line selection buttons and are linked through accessible descriptions; arrow-key selection and autosave retain their existing owner.

concepts.summary: Flower renders actor-native changes through the indexed ThreadCache and the published Floe incremental Markdown parser. Ordinary growth changes the affected text/DOM region only. A semantic change must remain visible; malformed updates recover through the single [live-state boundary](flower-live-timeline.md), never by omitting output or substituting a second lifecycle.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Local data and rendering
A snapshot initializes indexed item/message records once.

Obsolete JSON signature helpers and their signature-only tests are removed; projection tests assert canonical public fields directly. Actual removal transfers focus to an available adjacent action or composer unless navigation already moved it.

## One Markdown parser
Released Floe `createIncrementalMarkdownParser` owns Marked, CJK and GFM syntax. Reset establishes a source baseline; append returns explicit changed blocks, inline regions or text appends; finish performs the authoritative complete parse and necessary correction.

See [code highlighting](flower-code-highlighting.md) and [inline media](flower-inline-media.md).

## Disclosure and layout
Composer autosizing and approval measurements listen to releasable font loading completion/error events. Disposal removes those listeners; an unsettled FontFaceSet.ready promise must never retain a detached surface.

Companion reads the newest relevant record and bounds its normalized Unicode output tail instead of scanning historical messages or formatting the complete growing answer.

## Interaction cadence and resources
One bounded frame queue applies native updates in order inside the host's reactive batch.

Copy timers start only on explicit copy and reset after 1.6 seconds; clipboard failure never reports success.

The opt-in real-Service qualifier builds the production renderer, freezes historical content and provider cadence, and records cumulative runtime plus all Electron process CPU, frame/input/click/output latency, allocations and wire bytes. It verifies canonical provider content and rendered content after timing.

The task's explicit CPU, latency, allocation, transfer and long-task thresholds are hard gates, separate from ordinary CI and the bounded main pre-push gate.

`ThreadCache` owns canonical summaries.

Each summary batch publishes once through existing title/revision rules to avoid repeated transcript invalidation.

concepts.title: Flower consecutive tool sequences
concepts.description: Compact tools and bounded thinking without hiding dialogue or taking over active reading.

frontmatter.description: Compact tools and bounded thinking without hiding dialogue or taking over active reading.
frontmatter.title: Flower consecutive tool sequences

concepts.summary:
Flower groups consecutive tool calls in the shared Desktop and Env App timeline.
Thinking after the first tool becomes an inline node in that sequence, including
thinking after the final tool. Older settled sequences collapse while the newest
sequence and active tools remain expanded.
When an answered input falls between work segments in a settled turn, each
settled tool sequence remains independently collapsed, including the newest
sequence. Active tools retain their existing disclosure behavior.
This is product presentation over existing published Floret facts; it introduces
no upstream contract, canonical summary or backend migration.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Boundaries and identity

A sequence needs at least two nodes from the same thread, turn and run, including
a tool call. One tool plus following thinking qualifies. Successful, active and
failed calls and argument previews qualify. Running attention does not break a
sequence; waiting and approval do. Leading thinking stays standalone; thinking
from the first tool onward joins. Counts report calls, thinking segments and
failures without generating summaries. A newer single-call segment can make an
older untouched sequence eligible for collapse.

Prose, user messages, interactions, parent events, compaction, Goal state updates,
SubAgent operations, approvals, uncertain effects and non-tool errors break
sequences. Goal calls and Web Search remain tool nodes. Failed calls retain their
errors; summaries show the failure count and existing warning treatment. Whole-turn
disclosure stays separate, and grouping preserves source order and final output.
An answered input receipt is a turn-sequence boundary. When one splits a settled
turn's work, settled sequence groups on both sides default to collapsed; explicit
user choices and active calls continue to use the existing disclosure store.

Empty assistant text placeholders between tool messages are transparent; non-empty
text remains a boundary. Canonical tool identity owns row lifetime, the first call
anchors the sequence through updates, and thinking changes presentation in place.
Existing actions and details remain intact. Adjacent tool icons connect; theme
tokens own active, completed and failure states.

## Disclosure and reading

Choices live for the interface session by runtime, thread and tool. Automatic
collapse settles once; explicit choices persist through updates, reconnects and
navigation, then reset on refresh. Focus, selection, gestures, open details or
thinking, and reading away from the tail protect expansion.

Collapsed groups stay mounted and inert so nested detail state survives. Whole-turn
closure releases its body after motion. The timeline remains the sole scroll owner;
manual collapse restores focus to the group button, while automatic collapse above
the reader preserves position and user scrolling takes precedence.

Controls expose viewport IDs, localized counts and labels. Hidden nodes create no
gaps. Focus, reduced motion, forced colors, narrow layouts and pointer targets
follow shared Flower rules; both product catalogs translate all copy.

context, infer effects or persist lifecycle state. Published upstream components
and the canonical timeline own behavior. See [activity interaction](flower-activity-interaction.md)
and [whole-turn disclosure](flower-turn-process-disclosure.md).

concepts.summary:
Published Floret owns turn identity, outcome, final output and durations. Flower
uses validated detail only. Successful ordinary turns default to collapsed; the
latest failed, cancelled or interrupted turn stays expanded, while older
abnormal turns collapse after newer work starts. Dialogue, answered inputs and
final segments stay ordered and visible; unknown output is never hidden. Pending
interactions stay expanded, and reading protection preserves the reader's
position. If an answered input falls between process rows in a settled turn,
Flower shows a static overview and keeps the receipt as a visible checkpoint.
Settled tool sequences on either side default to independent collapsed groups;
active tools remain available. Ordinary turns keep whole-turn disclosure.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Canonical facts and eligibility
ThreadView and HistoryPage expose `turns`: exact TurnID and RunID, optional control kind, start and terminal time, outcome, elapsed/wait/work milliseconds, explicit ordered `intermediate_item_ids`, `final_item_ids` and `final_boundary_complete`. Summary updates cannot author them or trigger collapse.

The summary shows at most two nonzero time units, with subsecond copy; expansion reveals the original process without extra timing rows. A static overview for an interleaved answer also reports tool calls, failed calls, and answered input count; it never acts as a disclosure control.

## Reading and interface state
Running, preparing, retrying, finalizing and waiting turns remain expanded without a turn disclosure control. The latest ordinary turn retains process output, open thinking previews and details by default on failure, interruption or cancellation; users may then manually hide confirmed intermediate prose and explicitly typed process rows.

Main, embedded and child-detail timelines share the same renderer while using separate scroll controllers.

## Layout and accessibility
Messages and events share canonical Path ordering; timestamps never insert receipts.

Clarification receipts keep their existing secret-answer redaction.

sections.title: Contract

## Inline file inspection

Filtering, removing a file, changing sections, or switching commits cannot leave a detached old file object as the displayed diff.

The viewport remains contained at narrow widths and under Workbench projection.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
